item.title: Clickable Table of Contents for Case Files and Tenders
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: In a multi-part file the reader must reach the right section in seconds. How to add a contents page and bookmarks while merging.
item.content:encoded:
A case file, a tender bid, an accounting folder, thesis appendices: they all share a problem. Dozens of documents end up in one file and the reader cannot tell which page holds the annex they need. The fix is to add a contents page and bookmarks while you merge.

What you get

  • One PDF with your files merged in the order you pick
  • A contents page at the front listing each section and its starting page
  • A click on any line jumps to that section's first page
  • Bookmarks in the PDF reader's side panel
  • Optional: a Page 3 / 42 footer on every page and a Back to contents link at the start of each section

Step by step

  1. Add the files — Choose 2 to 20 PDFs, up to 50 MB each. Every file becomes a card with a thumbnail and its page count.
  2. Put them in order — Drag the cards or move them with the arrows; use Sort A-Z to order by name.
  3. Edit the titles — The default title is the file name with underscores and dashes turned into spaces. Write something meaningful to the reader, such as Annex 1 Lease Agreement.
  4. Choose the settings — Set the heading, numbering, footer and back link, and change the output file name.
  5. Merge and download — If the contents run long they continue onto the next page automatically, and section page numbers are calculated to match.

Merge + Table of Contents — Merge PDFs and add a clickable contents page and bookmarks; your files never leave your device. Open the tool

Writing titles that work

File names are often written for computers: scan_0047. A contents page is for a person. Use short titles that say what the item is, like Annex 3 Bank guarantee letter. Very long titles are cut to two lines at most, so put the main idea first.

When page sizes are mixed

A4, Letter and landscape pages keep their own size, while the contents page is added as portrait A4. The annexes are not altered; one uniform contents page simply appears at the front.

Protected or damaged files

A password-protected PDF cannot be handled in the browser, and the tool tells you exactly which file it is. Remove the password and add it again. A file that cannot be read does not block the others; its card is flagged and it is left out of the merge.

A court or an agency may have its own format requirements. If so, check the notice or guidance before you send the file.

item.title: Adding a QR Code to a PDF: Size, Placement, Print
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Adding a QR code to a PDF is easy; making it scan reliably is a matter of settings. Practical sizes, colours and print advice.
item.content:encoded:
You already have a finished PDF and want readers to land on a web page, a contact card or a Wi-Fi network. A QR code is the shortest route there, but dropping one onto the page at random can leave you with a square nobody can scan.

Step by step: putting a QR code on a PDF

  1. Pick the PDF — Drop your document into the tool. A thumbnail of the page appears as a preview.
  2. Enter the content — Choose website, contact card, phone, email, WhatsApp, Wi-Fi or plain text. You do not need to type https://; the tool adds it.
  3. Place it — Drag the QR on the preview and resize it from its corner. Put it on the first page, the last, every page or just pages such as 1,3,5-7.
  4. Download — The file comes out as original-name_qr.pdf. The text, links and forms of your document stay as they were.

Add a QR Code to PDF — Drag the QR anywhere on the page; your file never leaves your device. Open the tool

How big should it be?

Small codes struggle to scan. The tool warns you below 15 mm, and even on a tight layout such as a business card that is a sensible floor. The more you put in the code the denser its pattern becomes, which makes it harder to read at the same size. A short web address instead of a long text is the biggest win in a small space.

Colour and background

  • A dark pattern on a light background is the safest pairing.
  • A light pattern on a dark background fails on many phones; the tool notices and warns you.
  • If the pattern and background are close in tone the code may not scan; you get a warning when contrast is low.
  • Do not squeeze the blank frame around the code; the reader needs it to recognise the code.

Why it stays sharp in print

The QR is drawn into the PDF as vector shapes rather than as a picture. Scale it up or down and its edges stay crisp, even on a brochure going to a print shop. If you need the code on its own, you can download it as PNG or SVG too.

Adding a logo

You can place a small logo in the middle. Because a logo hides part of the code, the tool raises error correction to its highest level automatically. Keep the logo small anyway and test the printed result with your phone.

On screen you may need to zoom in before a phone can read the code; that is a screen limit, not a flaw. Print a test copy before sending the job away.

A web-address code is clickable inside the PDF

When the content is a web address, the area under the QR also becomes a clickable link inside the PDF. Someone reading on screen can click it; someone holding a printout can point a phone at it.

item.title: Business Card QR Code: How to Make a vCard
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Let the QR on your business card go straight to a phone's contacts instead of a web page. What a vCard is and how to prepare one.
item.content:encoded:
Business cards change hands, yet the number on them often never reaches the contacts list. Put a contact-card (vCard) QR code on the card and the other person can point their phone at it and save you in a tap.

What is a vCard QR code?

A QR with a web address opens a page. A contact-card QR stores the name, company, title, phone, email, website and address inside the code itself, and the person scanning can add them straight to their contacts. Nobody has to type or browse.

What goes in it?

  • First and last name
  • Company and job title
  • Mobile number
  • Email
  • Website
  • Address (optional)

You do not have to fill every field. The less you put in, the simpler the pattern, and the easier it is to read on a small card.

Accented characters

Letters such as ç, ğ, ı, İ, ö, ş and ü are encoded as UTF-8 when the contact card is written, so your name and address arrive in the contacts list intact. Scan your own card with your phone before printing to confirm the name looks right.

  1. Open your card PDF — Drop the business card PDF you plan to print or share into the tool.
  2. Choose the contact-card tab — Enter your details; the phone number and web address are tidied up for you.
  3. Place it in a free corner — Drag the QR to a spot that does not spoil the design. Even on a small card, stay at 15 mm or above.
  4. Download and test — Download the file and scan it with your own phone from the screen or a printout.

Add a QR Code to Your Card — Place a contact-card QR on your PDF; your file never leaves your device. Open the tool

Checklist before printing

  • Is the QR at least 15 mm?
  • Is the dark pattern on a light background?
  • Is there a blank frame around it?
  • Do the name, number and email look right when scanned?
  • Does a printed test copy scan too?

If your phone number or email changes, the code on printed cards goes stale, because the details are written into it. For details that change often, a web page address you can keep up to date is safer than a contact card.

item.title: Sales Representative CV Example
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: In a sales representative CV, write results rather than a duty list. Summary, bullet and skills examples inside.
item.content:encoded:
The most common mistake in a sales representative CV is listing duties instead of results. Employers want to see how well you did the job, not just that you were assigned it. This guide shows how to write the profile summary, work-experience bullets and skills section for a sales representative role, with examples you can copy and adapt.

Order and length

Put your name, title and contact details at the top, a short profile summary beneath, then work experience, education and skills. With little experience (recent graduate, internship) move education and projects ahead of work history. One page is enough for most applications; a second page is acceptable beyond roughly ten years of experience.

Applicant tracking systems (ATS) read plain, single-column CVs with standard headings (Summary, Experience, Education, Skills) best. Pick a more designed template for the version you hand to a recruiter.

Profile summary examples for a sales representative

Keep it to two to four sentences: years of experience, strengths and goal. Take one draft below and replace each [X] with your own information:

  • Goal-driven sales professional who understands customer needs and builds lasting relationships to consistently exceed targets.
  • I bring [X] years of field and in-store sales experience and I am strong in persuasion, relationship management and follow-up.
  • I see selling as a relationship built on trust: I listen to customers, recommend the right solution and stay in touch after the sale.
  • A competitive, disciplined sales consultant used to working with targets, I value keeping existing customers as much as winning new ones.
  • With solid product knowledge, strong communication and a results-driven approach, I want to add value to a new sales team and perform quickly.

Work-experience bullets for a sales representative

Start each bullet with an action and, where you can, include a number: how many people, items, what percentage, how fast. Wherever you see [X] below, insert your own real figure; if you don't know it, leave that bullet out.

  • Exceeded the monthly sales target by an average of [X]%
  • Managed and renewed a portfolio of [X] active customers
  • Grew revenue by [X]% through new customer acquisition
  • Prepared proposals and led pricing negotiations
  • Resolved customer complaints and raised repeat purchases
  • Reported sales figures regularly to management
  • Found new leads through cold calls and field visits
  • Prepared product presentations and demos tailored to customer needs
  • Beat sales targets during campaign and discount periods
  • Raised customer satisfaction with after-sales follow-up calls
  • Contributed to the sales strategy with competitor and market analysis
  • Helped train and onboard new sales team members

Only write what you actually did. If you couldn't explain a bullet in an interview, it shouldn't be on your CV.

item.title: How to Tailor Your CV to a Job Ad: A Keyword Guide
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: The words an ad uses often need to appear in your CV too. How to find what's missing and add it without making anything up.
item.content:encoded:
Sending the same CV to every ad is easy, but it is often the least effective approach. The ad describes what the employer wants in its own words; if your CV describes the same thing in different words, both the human reader and the applicant tracking system can miss it.

1. Read the ad carefully, once

Note the required qualifications ("at least 3 years", "Excel", "driving licence") separately from the nice-to-haves. Words that repeat show the employer's priorities. Read the requirements and duties, not the company blurb.

2. Match what you have to the ad's language

If an experience of yours meets a requirement, describe it with the ad's own word. If the ad says "stakeholder management" and you wrote "liaising with departments", and the work you did is genuinely the same, use the ad's wording.

A simple rule: never add a skill or experience just because the ad mentions it. Nothing should be on your CV that you couldn't explain in an interview.

3. See what's missing

Paste the ad into the job matcher in CV Maker's Analysis tab. It pulls out the ad's keywords and shows which appear in your CV and which don't. Word forms are matched by stem, so "managed" and "management" are treated alike. It all runs on your device; neither the ad nor your CV is sent to a server.

  • Add the missing keywords you genuinely have to your CV.
  • Don't add ones you don't have; say honestly in a cover letter that you are keen to learn.
  • Use a keyword once, in context, within the relevant bullet rather than repeating it.

4. Tailoring with AI (Pro)

The "Tailor to a job ad" feature in CV Maker's AI tab reads the ad together with your CV's experience and skills text and proposes a summary and bullet rewrites. Nothing overwrites your original: the suggestions you pick are applied to a separate copy of your CV.

Two safeguards guard against invention: a suggestion containing a number that isn't in your CV is rejected, and any tool or concept that isn't in your CV is flagged for you. When the AI can't find something, it asks you rather than making it up.

Your name, email, phone, address and photo are never sent to the AI — only experience, education and skills text. You can see exactly what is sent in the interface.

CV Maker — Paste the ad, see the missing keywords and adjust a copy of your CV to it. Tailor my CV

5. Keep a copy per application

CV Maker stores up to 12 CVs on your device. Keep your master CV intact and create a copy for each application, named after the company or role, so you can find which version went where.

6. Final checks before sending

  1. Check your dates — The Analysis section in CV Maker works out whether your job dates overlap or leave gaps, so you don't have to.
  2. Can screening software read your CV? — Employers often run CVs through screening software (an ATS) first; the ATS X-ray shows how your PDF looks to it.
  3. Page count — If the CV spills onto a second page, "Fit to one page" can bring it back to one.

item.title: What Is a Europass-Style CV and When Should You Use It?
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: The date-column layout common in Europe shows your career path at a glance. When is it a good choice and what should you watch for?
item.content:encoded:
Europass is a CV and documents framework developed by the European Union, and its official site offers an online CV editor. The "Europass-style" layout described here is not that official template; it is inspired by it: dates on the left, duties and details on the right.

Why the layout works

Your eye runs down the date column and sees the sequence of your career and any gaps at once. That is why it is popular for academic, public-sector, legal, healthcare and international applications.

When it fits

  • International, Erasmus, scholarship and research programme applications.
  • Long, steady careers where a clear timeline is a strength.
  • Traditional fields such as the public sector, academia, law and healthcare.

If the institution asks for a specific template or the official Europass format, follow that. The layout in this tool does not produce an official Europass file.

Preparing it

  1. Put your latest role first; give each entry a clear date range, position and organisation.
  2. Write 2–4 bullets per role and describe outcomes with numbers where you can.
  3. Keep education and languages short; use one consistent scale for language levels.
  4. Whether to include a photo depends on the country; follow local practice unless the ad says otherwise.

Which templates does CV Maker offer?

CV Maker has three date-column templates: Europass Style, Dated Serif and Dated Teal. All are for Pro members; you can change the colour, typeface and heading style.

In the date-column layouts the content is written to the PDF first, so the text order isn't scrambled; the ATS X-ray may still flag the layout as multi-column. For a CV you'll upload to an applicant tracking system a single-column template can be safer; look at the X-ray result and decide for yourself.

item.title: How to Write a Cover Letter: Structure and Tips
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: A good cover letter doesn't repeat the CV; it says what the CV doesn't. A four-paragraph structure.
item.content:encoded:
A cover letter is the short letter alongside your CV where you answer "why this job, why me". Rather than repeating the CV, it puts it in context.

A four-paragraph structure

  1. Opening: say which role you're applying for and what interests you, in a sentence or two.
  2. Evidence: link one or two requirements from the ad to a concrete result from your CV, with numbers and context.
  3. Motivation: why this company or role, and what it adds for you.
  4. Close: state that you'd welcome an interview, thank the reader and refer to your contact details.

Length and tone

Stay within one page; about 250–350 words is enough for most applications. Be warm but professional, and if you know the reader's name use it instead of a generic greeting.

What to avoid

  • Repeating your CV sentence by sentence.
  • Generic lines that could go to any company.
  • Claiming work you haven't done or skills you don't have.
  • Typos: read it aloud before sending.

A PDF in the same design as your CV

item.title: How to Take an ID Photo at Home: 8 Tips
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: You can shoot an ID photo with your phone without visiting a studio. Getting light, distance and pose right decides most of the result.
item.content:encoded:
When an application needs a photo in a hurry, visiting a studio can take time. A phone shot at home is a good start when the light and pose are right, and the background and size are easy to fix afterwards. For official documents such as ID and passports, check the current photo requirements of the authority.

Eight tips before you shoot

  1. Use window light: face the window so soft light falls on you; use a curtain to soften harsh sun.
  2. Pick a plain wall: stand before a light, patternless wall. The background can be changed later, but a plain one improves the result.
  3. Fix the phone: at eye level, propped up or held by someone. Shooting from above or below distorts the face.
  4. Keep your distance: about 1.5–2 metres away; very close shots enlarge the nose and forehead. Cropping in afterwards looks more natural.
  5. Use the rear camera: the front camera is lower quality and can distort; use a timer.
  6. Look straight into the lens: head level, shoulders square, neutral expression, eyes open.
  7. Keep hair and face clear: hair over the forehead or ears, glasses glare and a shiny forehead cause trouble.
  8. Take several: pick the best frame, with no blink and a natural expression.

After the shoot

item.title: How to Write a CV: A Step-by-Step Guide
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: A good CV is not the one that says everything, but the one that shows the right things quickly. A step-by-step roadmap from section order to how to word each bullet.
item.content:encoded:
Recruiters tend to spend very little time on a first read of a CV, so the useful information has to be easy to find. A good CV doesn't list everything you've done; it puts the items most relevant to the role up front. These steps give you a simple route when starting from scratch.

1. Start with the target

Instead of sending the same CV to every posting, read the job ad and note the skills it asks for. Move the matching experience and skills up and shorten the rest. This doesn't mean rewriting the CV each time; adjusting order and emphasis is enough.

2. Put the sections in the right order

  1. Header: name, target title, phone, email, city. Add a LinkedIn or portfolio link if you have one.
  2. Profile summary: two to four sentences — who you are, how many years in which field, and what you're looking for.
  3. Work experience: newest first. For each entry give title, company, dates and two to four bullets.
  4. Education: before experience if you are a recent graduate, after it if you are experienced.
  5. Skills, languages, certifications: choose those relevant to the ad; don't list hundreds of tool names.

3. Write results, not duties

“Prepared sales reports” describes a duty; “Improved stock planning with weekly sales reports, cutting waste by 12%” describes a result. If you don't have a figure, give the scale: team size, number of customers, budget. Start each bullet with an action verb and keep it to one or at most two lines.

Don't invent numbers. When there's no exact figure, “about” or a range is honest and enough; assume you will be asked about it in the interview.

4. Length and look

  • One page is usually enough for a few years of experience; two is reasonable for a long career.
  • Use at most two typefaces and a single accent colour. Generous white space reads better than dense text.
  • Be consistent: date format, bullet style and capitalisation should be the same throughout.

5. Should you include a photo?

In Turkey a CV photo is common and many employers expect it. When applying to other countries (for example the US or UK) a photo is usually left out; follow local practice unless the ad says otherwise. If you include one, choose a sharp, professional shot against a plain background.

CV Maker — Pick a template, type your details on the right and watch the CV build live on the left. Sections you leave empty are not added to the PDF. Build your CV

6. Save as PDF and name the file

  1. Download as a PDF — A PDF looks the same on every device; a Word file can break with different fonts or page sizes.
  2. Name the file clearly — Something like first-last-cv.pdf. “CV_final_final2.pdf” tells the employer nothing.
  3. Check the text is selectable — If you can select text with the mouse in the PDF, hiring systems can read it too.

Finally, show your CV to a friend and ask what they remember after 30 seconds. If it isn't what you want to stand out, change the order.

item.title: LinkedIn Profile Photo: Size and 7 Tips
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Your profile photo is one of the first things people see on LinkedIn. Practical tips for size, framing and background.
item.content:encoded:
Your profile photo is among the first things people see on LinkedIn. A good one makes your profile look more trustworthy and approachable. It doesn't need a big budget; attention to framing, light and background is enough.

Size

LinkedIn uses a square slot and displays the photo as a circle. According to LinkedIn's help pages the photo should be at least 400×400 pixels and under 8 MB; an 800×800 pixel square is comfortably enough. Because it's cropped round, keep your face in the centre and nothing important in the corners.

Seven tips

  1. Let the face fill about 60% of the frame — not too far, not too close.
  2. Keep it sharp: blurry or pixelated photos reduce trust.
  3. A natural smile makes you look approachable.
  4. Plain background: light grey or light blue keeps attention on your face.
  5. Professional but personal clothing: appropriate for your industry and simple.
  6. Only you: don't crop a group photo.
  7. Current: look like you do today; an old photo surprises people at interviews.

Preparing it

  1. Shoot in window light in front of a plain wall — Fix the phone at eye level and use the rear camera.
  2. Choose “LinkedIn profile (800×800)” in AI Photo Studio — The face is found, centred and cropped to the right proportion.
  3. Pick a background — Light blue or light grey gives a corporate look; you can also apply a blurred background.
  4. Download and upload to LinkedIn — Save as JPG; the size limit is rarely an issue.

item.title: What Makes a Good CV Photo? Size, Background, Framing
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: The first impression often starts with the photo. Practical standards for framing, background, light and size, and the mistakes people make most.
item.content:encoded:
The photo on a CV is a recruiter's first meeting with you. A well-chosen one builds trust; a careless one can overshadow everything else. You don't need a studio: the right light, a plain background and good framing make a phone photo work.

What a good CV photo looks like

  • Framing: head and shoulders (down to chest level). The face should fill about half the frame — not tiny, and not touching the edges.
  • Gaze: toward the camera at eye level. A slight, natural smile usually builds trust.
  • Background: plain and simple — light grey, light blue or white. A cluttered room or holiday scenery distracts.
  • Light: soft window light on your face is ideal. Backlight darkens the face; direct flash causes glare.
  • Clothing: suited to the industry, simple and solid. Busy patterns distract.
  • Recency: recent, and looking like you do today.

Common mistakes

  • Using a cropped group or holiday photo (someone's arm on your shoulder still shows).
  • Filters and heavy retouching that make you unrecognisable.
  • Very low resolution that looks blurry on the CV.
  • A side-on or tilted pose.
  • A coloured, busy background mixed with daylight.

Size and file

Most CV templates use a 3:4 portrait or a square slot. Prepare the photo in a ratio close to the slot to avoid awkward cropping. Around 300 KB is plenty; the image is reduced when embedded in the PDF anyway.

  1. Take the photo — Face a window, stand in front of a plain wall and hold the phone steady at eye level.
  2. Choose the “CV portrait” size in AI Photo Studio — AI finds your face, centres it and sets the head at the right proportion; you can make the background light grey or light blue.
  3. Read the suitability list and download — Check the warnings for light, head size and pose; download as JPG.

item.title: ATS-Friendly CV: 9 Practical Rules
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Many companies run CVs through an applicant tracking system first. Nine practical rules to make sure it reads yours completely.
item.content:encoded:
Many companies collect applications through an applicant tracking system (ATS). These systems read your CV and split the information into fields; anything they can't read, or place wrongly, looks incomplete on the recruiter's screen. A CV that looks beautiful but can't be read by a machine can be an invisible CV. These rules are practical ways to avoid that.

File and text

  1. Use a PDF that contains real text. Text in a CV saved as a screenshot or scanned image may not be read. If you can select text in the PDF with your mouse, you're on the right track.
  2. Don't bury information in images. Phone, email and skills should be text, not part of a logo or graphic.
  3. Choose standard fonts. Common, readable fonts are safest for people and systems alike; make sure Turkish characters (ş, ğ, ı, İ) display fully.

Structure and headings

  1. Use familiar headings: “Work Experience”, “Education”, “Skills”. Creative headings (“My Journey”) can stop a system recognising the section.
  2. Prefer a simple layout. Some systems read multi-column, table or boxed designs in the wrong order. If unsure, choose a single-column template.
  3. Write dates consistently, such as “Mar 2020 – Present”. Give every entry a title, company and date.

Content

  1. Use the ad's keywords naturally. If the ad says “project management” and you have that experience, use the same phrase — but never list a skill you don't have just to add a word.
  2. Spell out abbreviations once: “Customer Relationship Management (CRM)”. People and systems recognise both forms.
  3. Don't put key details in the page header or footer. Some systems skip those areas; place your contact details in the main body.

ATS behaviour varies from system to system and none guarantees a perfect read everywhere. The aim is to present information so that both people and machines read it easily.

CV Maker — The text in our templates is written to the PDF as selectable real text, not an image. For the simplest layout try the Plain template. Pick a template

A one-minute check before you send

  • Open the PDF, select all (Ctrl+A) and paste into a text editor: do the order and content make sense?
  • Are your phone and email written plainly in the header?
  • Is the file name clear, like first-last-cv.pdf?

item.title: Biometric Photo Sizes and Rules by Country (2026)
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Don't get your ID, passport or visa photo rejected: sizes, head proportions, backgrounds and the usual mistakes by country in one post.
item.content:encoded:
A biometric photo is an official document photo taken to specific size and rules so that face-recognition systems can use it too. A small deviation in size, background or head proportion can get an application rejected. The list below summarises common sizes.

Common sizes

  • Turkey (ID card, passport, driving licence): 50×60 mm, plain white background; the face covers roughly 70–80% of the photo.
  • Schengen and EU countries: 35×45 mm; head height about 32–36 mm; light, plain background.
  • United Kingdom: 35×45 mm; head height about 29–34 mm.
  • United States: 2×2 in (51×51 mm); head height about 25–35 mm; white background.
  • Canada: 50×70 mm; head height about 31–36 mm.
  • China (visa): 33×48 mm; white background.

Rules differ by country and change over time. The above is general information; always check the current requirements of the authority or consulate you apply to.

Basic rules that apply almost everywhere

  • Facing the camera straight on; head not tilted or turned.
  • Neutral expression, mouth closed, eyes open.
  • Shadow-free, plain, light background; no glare on face or eyes.
  • No hat, hair or accessories covering the face; the glasses rule varies by country and most applications want none.
  • No digital filters or retouching that alters facial features.
  • Recent photo (usually within the last 6 months).

How to prepare the photo

  1. Shoot in front of a plain wall — In window light, facing the camera at eye level, with the phone fixed in place.
  2. Choose the size — In AI Photo Studio pick a preset such as “Turkey biometric (50×60)”, “Schengen” or “US”; the head proportion is set automatically.
  3. Make the background white — AI separates the background down to strands of hair; apply white or light grey.
  4. Read the suitability list — Warnings for head size, expression and light are shown; retake if needed.
  5. Set a size limit if required — Portals may cap file size in KB; enter the maximum and the tool fits the file.

item.title: Can AI Review a Contract? How It Works and Where It Fails
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Handing a contract to an AI is easy. Knowing how far to trust the answer is the hard part. This is a plain account of the process, the safeguards and the limits.
item.content:encoded:
Whether an AI contract review is useful depends less on the model than on the process around it. Here is what the Contract Auditor does with your document, what stops it from inventing things, and the places where you should not rely on it.

What happens to your document

  1. Text is extracted on your device — The PDF itself is not uploaded. Only its text is sent for analysis, and scanned pages are read on your device with OCR first.
  2. The document is identified and you answer a few questions — The system works out the document type and the parties, then asks questions whose answers change the analysis. You say which side you are on; it does not guess.
  3. The analysis runs — A quick scan finds the main risks in one pass. A detailed audit reads the document several times, calculates figures, looks up legal points in official sources and puts the findings through a second check.
  4. The result appears in the document — Risky passages are highlighted in your PDF. Each finding gives the reason and the impact, and the detailed audit adds suggested replacement wording.

Four safeguards against made-up findings

  1. Every finding carries a word-for-word quote, and software searches for that quote in the document. A finding whose quote cannot be found never reaches the report.
  2. Page numbers come from where the quote really sits in the document, not from the model's estimate.
  3. In the detailed audit, statute articles are never written from the model's memory. Only text read from an official source is shown, with a link, and anything that could not be read is marked 'could not verify'.
  4. What the system does not know is listed openly in an assumptions section.

Where it can still fail

  • It can be wrong, either missing a risk or overstating one. The output is a preliminary assessment, not legal advice.
  • It cannot judge what it has not seen. An annex that is not in the file cannot be analysed, and the report says so.
  • Only the detailed audit checks current law; the quick scan gives no statutory basis.
  • Very long documents (above roughly 240,000 characters) have to be split, and for scans the first 30 pages are read.

Choosing between the two modes

Use the quick scan for a first look. It takes about 1 to 2 minutes and uses 8 to 20 units depending on length, drawn from the monthly allowance first and then from credits. Use the detailed audit for a contract you are about to sign. It takes about 6 to 12 minutes and uses 85 to 122 credits, from purchased credits only. It costs more because the strongest model reads the document several times and checks legal points against official sources.

Privacy and retention

Document text is not stored on our servers, and the result is deleted within 30 minutes. Our AI provider does not use API data to train models by default; it may keep it for up to 30 days for safety review only. The result lives only on the page where the analysis finished, so download the report straight away.

item.title: Late-Delivery Penalty Calculator: Clause Into Numbers
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: A rate of 0.5% per day looks small until you multiply it out. This guide shows the arithmetic, where the traps hide and what to ask for before signing.
item.content:encoded:
Most delay clauses fit in one line: 'for each day of delay, a given percentage of the contract price'. The line is short and the consequence can be large, so before you sign it is worth doing the sum once and seeing where the clause could take you.

The formula

Penalty = base amount x daily rate x days late. On a 1,000,000 TL contract at 0.5% per day, each day costs 5,000 TL. Twenty days is 100,000 TL, which is 10% of the price. The same 10% arrives in ten days if the rate is 1% instead.

How fast common rates add up

  • 0.1% per day: 1% after 10 days, 10% after 100 days.
  • 0.5% per day: 10% after 20 days, 50% after 100 days.
  • 1% per day: 10% after 10 days, the full price after 100 days.

Three questions that change the result

  1. Is there a cap? A sentence such as 'total penalties shall not exceed 10% of the contract price' is the single most useful protection. Without it the penalty can reach the whole price and beyond, and if the contract also lets the other side claim damages in addition, the clause is uncapped in practice.
  2. What is the base? 'Contract price' may mean the VAT-inclusive price, the VAT-exclusive price or only the delayed portion. If the contract does not say, expect the other side to pick the biggest figure; a VAT-inclusive base gives a penalty 20% higher than a VAT-exclusive one.
  3. Whose delay is it? If your deadline depends on an approval, sample or document the other side must provide, their delay should not count against you. Look for an extension clause for delays they cause, and ask for one if it is missing.

Contract Auditor — Uses the price you enter to convert penalty rates into money, and tells you plainly when no cap exists or deadlines conflict with an annex. Open the tool

Do not count on a court to reduce it

There is a general principle that a court may reduce an excessive penalty, but commercial matters between merchants fall under a separate rule where that room may be limited. If you are a merchant, negotiating a heavy clause before signing is far safer than hoping to have it trimmed afterwards. Check the current wording at an official source such as mevzuat.gov.tr; this article is not legal advice.

Two requests are often accepted: a cap on total penalties, and mutuality, meaning a matching penalty or interest when the other side pays late.

item.title: Contract Review Checklist: 12 Clauses Before You Sign
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Contracts rarely go wrong in the long, complicated clauses. They go wrong in a deadline buried in an annex or a termination right that only one side has. Twelve checks, grouped by what they protect.
item.content:encoded:
If you have ever lost a dispute over a contract you had technically read, the cause was probably small: a different delivery date in an annex, a penalty with no ceiling, a right to terminate that belonged to the other party alone. This checklist groups twelve checks by what they protect, so you can work through a contract in a fixed order instead of rereading it hoping to notice something.

Group 1: Who is bound, and to what

  1. Parties and authority. Company names, tax numbers, and whether the person signing can actually bind the company.
  2. Subject and scope. What is delivered, in what quantity and to what standard. Phrases such as 'reasonable time' or 'as deemed necessary' are where arguments begin.
  3. Price and payment. VAT included or excluded, the payment term and the date it starts from. If invoicing waits for an approval, check whether that approval has its own deadline.
  4. Deadlines and notices. Delivery, objection, notice and non-renewal periods, and for each one who must notify whom and by what means (notary, email, registered post).

Group 2: What it costs when things go wrong

  1. Late-delivery penalty. The rate, whether there is a cap, and the amount it is applied to. If damages can be claimed on top of the penalty, treat the penalty as uncapped.
  2. Termination. Can both sides terminate? With how much notice? Is work already performed paid for?
  3. Liability. How are indirect loss, lost profit and gross negligence handled, and is the cap offered to one party only?
  4. Intellectual property and confidentiality. Do your designs, tooling or methods pass to the other side, and are the confidentiality exceptions mutual?

Group 3: The structure around the text

  1. Annexes. Do you hold every annex the contract mentions? If a clause says the annex prevails over the body, read the annexes first.
  2. Term and renewal. Does the contract renew by itself, and by when must you give notice to stop that?
  3. Disputes. Which court or arbitral body, and which governing law? A distant forum makes enforcement more expensive.
  4. What is absent. Force majeure, transfer of risk, warranty and defect periods, assignment, data protection. Missing standard clauses are findings too.

Convert every rate into a number before you decide. '1% per day' reads as harmless; on a 2,400,000 TL job it is 24,000 TL every day.

Contract Auditor — Runs this checklist on your own document: it flags contradictions, works out penalty amounts and lists missing clauses, with the risky passages highlighted. Open the tool

Working order

Do groups 2 and 3 first. Penalty, termination, payment and liability carry the biggest money, and annex conflicts decide which of your figures even apply. For every clause you flag, note the problem and a balanced replacement the other side could realistically accept; a marked-up contract with fixes gets further than one with objections alone.

This is a screening aid, not legal advice. On a high-value or multi-year agreement, take a lawyer's view before signing, and bring your flagged list so the conversation starts where your own review stopped.

item.title: Tender Documents Risk Review: Check Before You Bid
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Submitting a bid means accepting everything in the specification and draft contract, usually without negotiation. The review therefore has to happen before the bid.
item.content:encoded:
In a tender the draft contract is normally take-it-or-leave-it. Your bid is treated as acceptance of the specification and the draft, so the real decision is made while you read the file, not when you sign. That makes the reading stage the place to spend your time.

Start with the documents against each other

A tender file typically holds an administrative specification, a technical specification, a draft contract and annexes. They are written by different people, and it is common for one to say 90 days and another 60. Find the clause that ranks the documents, and send a written clarification request for every conflict you find.

Eight points that carry the risk

  • Completion period and extensions: do force majeure and delays caused by the authority move the date?
  • Late penalty: daily rate, cap, and the amount it is calculated on.
  • Guarantees: size of the bid and performance bonds, when they are returned, when they are forfeited.
  • Payment: how often interim payments are made, the payment term, and whether late payment earns interest.
  • Price adjustment: is there any mechanism if input costs rise on a long job?
  • Variations: what limit applies when the authority increases or reduces the work?
  • Termination: when and how can the authority end the contract, and what does that cost you?
  • Missing annexes: documents the draft refers to that are not in the file.

Watch the precedence clause

Many drafts say which document wins if two conflict. That sentence can lift an innocent-looking line in an annex above the main contract, so read the annexes with it in mind.

Contract Auditor — Run the specification and draft contract through the 'Public tender' option to surface contradictions, penalty arithmetic and missing annexes. Open the tool

Rules change, so verify them

Public tenders in Turkey are governed by the Public Procurement Law, the Public Procurement Contracts Law and the regulations under them, and these are amended from time to time. When judging whether a provision is lawful, read the current text at official sources such as the Official Gazette, mevzuat.gov.tr and the Public Procurement Authority. For an important tender, legal support also helps you keep the objection and application deadlines.

Clarification and objection windows are short. Reading the file in the first days, not the last, leaves room both to ask questions and to decide whether to bid.

item.title: When a Contract Annex Contradicts the Main Text
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: The body says 45 days. The annex says 30. A single 'annexes prevail' sentence decides which one you are held to, and when your penalty starts.
item.content:encoded:
Long contracts say the same thing in several places: the main text, the technical specification, the price schedule. Most of the time they agree. When they do not, the question that matters is which one wins, and the answer often sits in a short precedence clause that few people read closely.

A conflict with a price tag

Clause 4 allows 45 days for delivery. The technical specification in Annex 1 says 30. Clause 13 reads: if the contract and its annexes conflict, the annexes prevail. The deadline is therefore 30 days. Deliver on day 45 and you are 15 days late, with the daily penalty already running.

The three situations you will meet

  • 'Annexes prevail': a detail in an annex can override the main text, so annexes deserve the same attention as the body.
  • 'The main text prevails': conflicting annex terms do not apply, though cleaning up the conflict is still safer.
  • No precedence clause: which one applies becomes a matter of argument, and that usually means a dispute.

A three-step way to find conflicts

  1. List the subjects — Note what the body fixes with numbers or names: period, price, penalty, payment term, parties, jurisdiction.
  2. Search the annexes for each one — Read how the same subject appears there. Figures, days and rates are where the differences are.
  3. Find the ranking clause — Locate the sentence saying which document wins, and apply it to every difference you found.

Contract Auditor — Finds conflicts between clauses and annexes, shows which would prevail under the ranking rule and what the difference costs. Open the tool

Before you sign

  1. Send the other side a written list of every conflicting place and agree on one figure for each.
  2. Rewrite the ranking clause into a balanced one, for example that the later-dated or more specific document prevails.
  3. Ask for and read any annex whose text you have not seen. An annex you were never shown can still bind you.

Two different jobs, two tools: Compare PDFs shows what changed between two versions of a contract, while the Contract Auditor looks for conflicts between the clauses and annexes inside one document.

Compare PDFs — See which clauses were added, removed or changed between two versions of a contract. Open the tool

item.title: From a UYAP Decision to Word: Two Routes and a Check
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Word cannot open a UDF and you cannot copy from it. The bridge is PDF, and the choice is whether you need the text only or the formatting too.
item.content:encoded:
You have a precedent decision and want a few paragraphs of its reasoning in your own filing. The file is a UDF, Word will not open it and you cannot copy from it. Most people end up retyping from the screen, but it transfers in two steps.

Why direct opening fails

UDF is UYAP's own document format and has nothing in common with the formats Word recognises. Renaming the extension to .doc does not help either, because that changes the name and not the structure inside the file.

The bridge is PDF. Convert the UDF to PDF and you have a widely supported document, and from there going to Word is a standard operation.

Which route

  • You only need the text: take the plain text (.txt) the UDF tool gives you and paste it into Word. This is the fastest route. Formatting does not come across, but the text does.
  • You need the formatting too: convert UDF to PDF, then PDF to Word. Paragraph layout, bold text and tables are preserved.

For quoting in a filing the first route is usually enough, since you will reformat the text to match your own document anyway. Choose the second when you need to carry a table or a layout across as it stands.

The formatted route in four steps

  1. Convert the UDF to PDF — Drop the file into the UDF tool. The work happens in your browser, and court documents are not uploaded.
  2. Download the PDF — Fonts, bold and underlined text, alignment and tables are preserved.
  3. Convert the PDF to Word — Feed the downloaded PDF to the PDF to Word tool and get an editable .docx.
  4. Check in Word — Review paragraph breaks and any tables after conversion. Small corrections in long documents are normal.

UDF to PDF — Convert a decision downloaded from UYAP to PDF with nothing installed, and take the text as .txt too. Open the tool

Scanned decisions need an extra step

In older case files a decision sometimes arrives not as a UDF but as a scanned image. The writing is then a picture, so you can neither copy nor search it. Run the document through OCR first to turn the image into real text, and the same steps then get you into Word.

Scanned PDF to Text (OCR) — Turn the writing inside a scanned decision into real text, then take it into Word. Open the tool

Verify against the original

No conversion is flawless, and in a legal text a single shifted digit has serious consequences. After transferring into Word, compare these against the original:

  • Case and decision numbers.
  • Dates.
  • Monetary amounts and interest rates.
  • Statutory article numbers.
  • The spelling of party names.

Keep the PDF of the decision as well. If you later need to show that your quotation is accurate, you have a readable copy of the source to hand.

The PDF is a copy, not the signed original

The electronic signature in a UDF does not carry into the PDF. The converted file is a readable copy for working and quoting. If an official filing needs the document, use the signed UDF original.

item.title: Hiding ID Numbers and Addresses Before You Share a File
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Official documents carry your identity number and address, and the recipient often does not need either. Covering them is not the same as removing them.
item.content:encoded:
An estate agent asks for proof of income. Your document carries your identity number, address, date of birth and salary. The agent needs only some of that, but sending the whole document is the easy option, so most people do exactly that. Once the details are out, they cannot be pulled back.

The common mistake: a black box

Most people draw a black rectangle over the detail in a PDF viewer. On screen the information disappears and the job looks done.

It is not. A box drawn on a PDF is a shape added on top of the document, and the text underneath stays exactly where it was. If the recipient selects that area and copies it, your identity number comes out intact, and that takes no technical skill.

Test it on your own document. Select the area you covered, copy it and paste into a text box. If the information appears, you have not redacted it, you have only covered it.

The same flaw applies to white boxes, highlighter strokes and images pasted over text. Invisible is not the same as deleted.

The right method

Real redaction removes the text from inside the document. Nothing remains in the covered area to copy, and searching returns nothing either.

  1. Add the document — Give the PDF to the redaction tool. If the text is searchable in the document, it works directly.
  2. Choose what to remove — Patterned data such as identity numbers, phone numbers and bank account numbers is found automatically. Tick the ones you want removed.
  3. Check and download — Your selections are stripped out of the document. In the downloaded file, try selecting and copying those areas, and nothing should come out.

Redact Sensitive Data — Truly remove identity numbers, bank details and addresses instead of painting over them. Open the tool

Scanned documents behave differently

If your document was scanned or photographed, the writing is an image and there is no selectable text layer. That is both good and bad news.

The good news is that the text cannot be copied anyway. The bad news is that it is still readable by eye, so you still need to cover it, and the covering has to be applied to the image itself. Zoom into the redacted area in the downloaded file to confirm it is genuinely covered.

What to hide for whom

Over-redacting makes a document useless, and under-redacting does not protect you. A practical rule: anything the recipient does not need for the task can be hidden.

  • A government body: usually hide nothing. They will verify your identity, and an incomplete document gets rejected.
  • An employer: the identity number is often required, but family details, home address and health data usually are not.
  • Private parties such as agents, sellers or websites: identity number and date of birth are almost never needed.
  • Anything you will post publicly: do not share the document at all, because even a redacted document carries details that can identify you.

Sometimes send one page instead

Sometimes the cleanest answer is not to redact but to send only the page that matters. Rather than sharing an eight-page statement with six pages blacked out, pull out the single relevant page and send that. It is safer, and it makes the recipient's job easier too.

item.title: UYAP Upload Rejected? The Size Checklist That Fixes It
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: The portal rarely tells you why a file was rejected, and the cause is usually the size of the scanned exhibits. Diagnose first, then shrink the right thing.
item.content:encoded:
The hearing is close, the petition is ready and the exhibits are scanned, but the portal will not take the file. UYAP, Turkey's national judiciary e-filing system, seldom says the problem is size, and a generic error invites endless retries. This guide separates the possible causes and shows how to get under the limit.

Find the cause before you fix anything

An upload failure has three common sources, and each needs a different fix:

  1. The size limit was exceeded. This is the most frequent cause, and it nearly always comes from scanned exhibits.
  2. The format is not accepted. The portal expects specific extensions, and uploading a phone photo directly is a common mistake.
  3. The file is corrupt or password protected. An encrypted PDF cannot be opened on the other side.

A fast test: upload a small, one-page test PDF. If that goes through, the problem is the size or content of your file. If it does not, the problem is on the portal's side and you will have to wait.

What inflates the file

The petition itself is a few hundred kilobytes. What pushes a filing into tens of megabytes is almost always the exhibits: pages scanned in colour at high resolution, or phone photos turned into a PDF. A modern phone camera saves a single page as a 4 to 6 MB image, so twenty pages easily pass 100 MB.

The answer is not to trim the petition. It is to bring the exhibits down to a sensible size, which can be done without losing legibility.

Getting under the limit

  1. Compress the file — Feed it to the compression tool and pick a level. Scanned, image-heavy documents gain the most, and most files drop to about a third.
  2. Check the result by eye — Open the downloaded file and look at the page with the smallest type. If it reads comfortably, you are fine. If it blurred, step down one compression level.
  3. Still too big? Split it — If a single file exceeds the limit, upload the petition and the exhibits as separate files, breaking the document into page ranges.
  4. Name the parts — Something like exhibit-1-expert-report.pdf. File names are the cheapest way to make the reader's job easier.

Compress PDF — Shrink scanned exhibits without hurting legibility and get under the portal's limit. Open the tool

Scan small in the first place

Scanning correctly beats compressing afterwards every time. For official paperwork:

  • Choose black and white or greyscale. Unless there is a coloured stamp or signature, you do not need colour, and colour triples the file.
  • 300 DPI is enough. Higher does not improve legibility, it only inflates the file.
  • On a phone, scan rather than photograph. A scanner finds the edges, corrects the perspective and produces a much smaller file.

Instead of turning a phone photo straight into a PDF, run it through the document scanner. Edges are detected automatically, the page is flattened, and the result looks scanned and is far smaller.

UDF files are a separate matter

UYAP's own document format, UDF, has its own tighter size limit on the system side. In practice UDF files above 10 MB are reported as rejected, and the system does not say so; it shows a generic error.

If your UDF is large, the cause is almost always images pasted into the document. Taking the images out and uploading them as separate exhibits is the cleanest fix. Limits differ by institution and filing type and change over time, so trust the note on the upload screen for the exact figure.

Four checks before you upload

  • Is the file password protected? An encrypted PDF cannot be opened on the other side, so remove the lock.
  • Are the pages in the right order and the right way up? A sideways exhibit makes the reader rotate the document.
  • Is there personal data that does not belong in this filing? Take it out.
  • Is the total size below the limit shown on screen?

These checks take a minute and prevent most last-day upload crises.

item.title: Visa Application Documents: A File an Officer Can Read
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Visa applications are often weakened not by a missing paper but by a messy file. A clean, ordered, legible set of documents helps your case.
item.content:encoded:
A visa application tells the story of a period of your life through documents: where you work, whether you have funds and whether you will return. An officer gives the file minutes, so jumbled, unreadable or apparently incomplete paperwork counts against you. Here is how to put it together properly.

Start with the current list

Every country and visa type asks for a different set of documents, and the lists change. Take the current list from the consulate's own page or the authorised application centre. Preparing from an old list found online is the most common mistake.

Then work through it item by item. A missing document outranks even a beautifully organised file.

Get each document in the right form

  • Download anything available from a government portal directly as a PDF. Do not screenshot it, because the verification barcode may not be readable.
  • Take bank statements from your bank's own app as PDFs. Screenshots are not accepted.
  • Scan paper documents such as a signed leave letter or an invitation rather than photographing them.
  • Scan passport pages sharply and fully in frame. A passport page with clipped corners is among the most frequently returned items.

Rather than turning a phone photo straight into a PDF, run it through a document scanner. Edges are detected, the page is flattened, and the desk, your fingers and shadows stay out of frame. The result looks scanned.

The photo is the item most often sent back

The biometric photo is the most frequently rejected item. In Turkey the common size for ID cards, passports and driving licences is 50 x 60 mm, while Schengen and many other visa applications ask for 35 x 45 mm.

Where a system wants a digital upload, both the pixel dimensions and the file size have to fit. You can resize the photo to hit the dimensions and compress it separately if the file is too large.

To be clear, bringing a photo to the right pixel size does not make it biometrically compliant. A plain white background, a centred and correctly proportioned face, open eyes and a neutral expression all depend on how the photo was taken. A resizing tool only sets the size.

Resize Image — Bring a photo to the pixel dimensions visa and biometric applications ask for, using ready-made sizes. Open the tool

Combining into one PDF

Some application centres want each document separately and others want a single file. If one file is wanted, order matters, so arrange the documents in the order given on the list.

  1. Add the documents in order — Application form, passport, photo, travel insurance, flights and accommodation, employment and financial documents. The consulate's own order is the safest.
  2. Check the order — Drag to rearrange in the list. A wrong order means the officer cannot find the document they are looking for.
  3. Merge and download — You get one PDF, and your files never leave your device.
  4. Check the size limit — If the upload screen states a limit and you are over it, compress; scanned pages give the biggest gain.

Open the file as a reader would

  • Is every page upright, or is something sideways?
  • Does the smallest text read comfortably? If you have to zoom, rescan it.
  • Does the page order match the list?
  • Has a document carrying personal data that was not asked for slipped in?
  • Is the file name clear? Something like visa-application-name-surname.pdf works well.

That check takes five minutes. Set against how long you waited for the appointment, going through the file once more is well worth it.

item.title: One Payroll PDF, Forty Payslips: Split Per Employee
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: The risk in payslip distribution is not time but mistakes. A split that is visual, fast and checked removes most of it.
item.content:encoded:
Payroll has sent the file, and you have a single PDF of forty pages for forty employees. Each person should receive only their own page. Saving and naming each page by hand takes half a day and carries a risk of mix-ups, and a mix-up here sends one employee's salary to someone else.

The real problem is error, not time

Salary information is among the most sensitive personal data there is, and reaching the wrong person cannot be undone. In a repetitive manual task, losing focus by the fortieth page is entirely normal. A method that does the job in one move brings the time down to minutes and removes the question of whether anything got mixed up.

Four steps

  1. Add the payroll file — Give the PDF to the split tool. The work happens in your browser, and salary data is not uploaded.
  2. Pick pages visually — Pages are listed as thumbnails, so you can confirm which page belongs to whom.
  3. Take each page as its own file — Pages are separated individually and downloaded in a ZIP, with each page as its own file.
  4. Name the files — Before sending, give each file the employee's name. This is your last defence against a misdirected email.

Split PDF — Break a combined payroll file page by page, on your device with nothing uploaded. Open the tool

When an employee spans several pages

In some payrolls a single employee takes two or three pages, and splitting page by page will not do. You need page ranges.

The split tool lets you choose ranges, such as pages 1 to 2 as one file and 3 to 4 as another. Thanks to the thumbnails you can confirm each range by eye, which is far safer than typing numbers blind.

Check before you send

Even when the split is correct, no tool can catch a slip in your sending list. Do these two checks first:

  • Open three files at random and confirm the name inside matches the file name.
  • Check that the number of files matches the number of employees. A file too few or too many means the ranges have slipped.

Do not send payslips as a group email. A single reply-all, or a wrongly chosen recipient list, can expose the whole company's salaries. Each payslip should go in its own email, to one recipient.

Where else this helps

  • Separating combined invoice files by customer.
  • Splitting bulk-generated certificates into one per person.
  • Sending the relevant sections of a long report to different departments.
  • Pulling only the signature page out of a long contract.

item.title: Exam Photo Rejected? Fix Pixel Size and File Size
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Application systems rarely tell you why a photo failed. It is nearly always the pixel dimensions, the file size, or both, and they are fixed separately.
item.content:encoded:
It is the last day of applications, the form is filled in and you have reached the photo. The system will not accept it, and the error is rarely informative. In almost every case the pixel dimensions or the file size do not match what was asked for.

A typical requirement

Turkish exam applications commonly ask for:

  • Pixel dimensions: 300 x 400 (width by height).
  • File size: 60 KB at most.
  • Format: JPG (JPEG).
  • Content: taken within the last six months, white background, face clearly visible.

These requirements differ between institutions and change from year to year. The note on the application screen always governs, and the method below works whatever size is asked for.

Pixels and kilobytes are different things

This distinction is the real source of the confusion. Pixel dimensions are the photo's width and height, such as 300 x 400. File size is how much room it takes on disk, such as 60 KB.

A photo can be exactly 300 x 400 pixels and still weigh 400 KB, and the reverse is possible too. Satisfy the two conditions separately: set the dimensions first, then compress if the size is still high.

Four steps

  1. Set the right dimensions — In the resize tool, pick the exam application entry from the ready-made sizes, which gives 300 x 400. You can also type the numbers in.
  2. Check the file size — Look at the size of the downloaded file. Under 60 KB and you are done.
  3. Compress if needed — If it is still large, put it through the image compressor and lower the quality gradually. At passport-photo dimensions, 70% quality usually drops under 60 KB while keeping the face sharp.
  4. Check by eye — Open the photo at full size and make sure the face is sharp. Over-compression distorts facial features and the photo may be rejected.

Resize Image — Bring a photo to the pixel dimensions exam and official applications require, with ready-made sizes and on your device. Open the tool

Crop before you resize. First crop to a 3:4 ratio with the face centred, then set 300 x 400. Do it the other way round and the face gets squashed out of proportion.

Common mistakes

  • Uploading an ordinary phone photo without cropping. Camera photos are 4:3 or 16:9, while a passport photo is 3:4, so crop to that ratio first.
  • Using a screenshot. Screenshots come out as PNG and are usually both the wrong size and heavier than needed.
  • Enlarging a small photo. Taking a 150 x 200 image up to 300 x 400 gives a blurry result, because lost detail does not come back.
  • Assuming the background is white. If the wall is light grey or cream, the system or a reviewer may reject it.

Other official photo sizes

The same method applies to every official photo size. In Turkey, ID card, passport and driving licence applications commonly use 50 x 60 mm, while Schengen and many other visa applications ask for 35 x 45 mm. Sizes given in millimetres convert to pixels at 300 DPI.

Worth repeating: a tool that brings a photo to the right size does not make it biometrically compliant. Background, the position of the face and the expression all depend on how the photo was taken.

item.title: Assembling a Tender Bid PDF: Order, Numbers, Signatures
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: In a tender, how the file is organised is the first thing the committee sees. A bid they can navigate quickly starts ahead of one they cannot.
item.content:encoded:
A tender bid is as much about organisation as about documents. A committee works through dozens of files in turn, and the one where things are easy to find has an advantage. Most authorities now want bids electronically, which leaves presenting them together, in order and legibly entirely to you.

The specification always wins

Nothing here overrides the instruction in the authority's own specification. If it states the order of documents, the file format, the naming or a size limit, follow it to the letter. Failing a formal requirement can be enough on its own to have a bid excluded.

The fastest approach is to download the specification and search it for file, format, PDF, signature and size, noting every clause that comes up.

Order the documents as the specification lists them

Tender specifications give the required documents as a numbered list. Build your file in exactly that order. A committee member works with the list in hand, and a file that follows the same sequence makes the review flow.

  1. Prepare each document as a PDF — Download anything from official portals directly as a PDF, and scan the paper documents.
  2. Arrange in specification order — In the merge tool, drag the files to match the numbering on the list.
  3. Combine into one file — The work happens in your browser, and your bid is not uploaded to a server.
  4. Add page numbers — With a numbered file, the committee can ask which page a document is on, and you can answer.

Merge PDF — Put bid documents in specification order and combine them into one file, on your device with no signup. Open the tool

Why page numbers help

In a hundred-page bid, page numbers make a table of contents possible. A contents page at the front, listing where each document begins, makes the committee's job markedly easier and makes your file look like careful work. Most competitors will not bother.

Add Page Numbers — Number the pages of a bid so a table of contents becomes possible. Open the tool

Size limits against scan quality

Electronic tender systems impose size limits, yet documents also have to be legible, because an unreadable document counts as a missing one. You have to balance the two.

  • Scan in greyscale at 300 DPI. If colour is not needed, do not use it, because it multiplies the file.
  • If there is a company stamp or a coloured signature, scan only those pages in colour and leave the rest grey.
  • After compressing, always check whether the stamp is readable, the signature is sharp and the smallest type is still legible.
  • If you are still over the limit, splitting the file is safer than lowering quality.

Never crush the whole file at maximum compression. An unreadable stamp in a tender file can lose work you had already won. Look at which pages are heavy first, since the problem is usually in a handful of them.

Signatures need care

Signatures are critical in bids, and authorities generally require a wet signature or a qualified electronic signature. Placing an image of a signature on a PDF meets neither requirement, because it is only a picture.

In practice the right route is to print, sign by hand and scan, or to use the electronic signature infrastructure the authority accepts. Image signatures suit informal situations such as internal correspondence and draft sharing.

A last check before you submit

  • Is every item on the specification's list present in the file?
  • Does the order match the specification?
  • Are time-limited documents such as registration and tax-clearance certificates current?
  • Is every page upright and legible?
  • Does the file name match what the authority asked for?
  • How many hours are left before the deadline? Do not leave the upload to the last hour, because system load is a real risk.

item.title: University Enrolment Documents the Portal Accepts First Time
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Enrolment week is short and the system is busy. Most rejected uploads trace back to how the document was captured, not to the document itself.
item.content:encoded:
Enrolment days are short and the system is busy, and you have a stack of documents: a school diploma, exam results, an ID copy, proof of address, a medical report and a photo. Most of it is uploaded digitally now. This guide covers how to prepare them so they are accepted first time.

Scan, do not photograph

This is the most common mistake. Photographing a document on a table is quick, but the result is usually rejected: the table shows, the edges are skewed, light hits one corner and the file is needlessly large.

A document scanner finds the edges, corrects the perspective and lays the paper down as a flat page. The result looks scanned and the file is far smaller, and you need no extra hardware because your phone camera is enough.

  1. Put the document on a flat surface — A dark surface makes the edges easier to find. Flatten the paper as much as you can.
  2. Light it from above, not the side — Keep your own shadow off the document. Window light is enough, and flash usually causes glare.
  3. Run the scanner — Edges are found automatically and the page is flattened. Adjust the corners by hand if needed.
  4. Save it as a PDF — You can gather several pages into one document.

Document Scanner — Scan properly with your phone: edges found, page flattened, file kept small. Open the tool

Do not scan what a portal can issue

Some documents need no scanning at all. Proof of address, civil registry extracts and criminal record certificates can be downloaded straight from a government portal as PDFs. A downloaded document is already digital, sharp and small, and it can be verified by the barcode on it. Printing and rescanning throws all of that away.

Do not take screenshots. Use the download as PDF option, because verification barcodes usually do not survive a screenshot and the document may be rejected.

The photo

The photo for a student card has specific pixel dimensions and a file size limit. A phone photo is both the wrong ratio and larger than needed, so crop to passport-photo ratio first and then set the required size. If the dimensions fit but the file is still large, compress it separately, since pixel dimensions and file size are different things and most systems require both.

One file or several

Universities usually have a separate upload field per document. If a single file is wanted, order the documents as the enrolment guide lists them.

Where a document runs to several pages, such as both sides of a diploma, merge them into one PDF before uploading, because systems often accept only one file per field.

If you hit the upload limit

  • Compress the scanned documents, since that is where the gain is.
  • Scan in greyscale rather than colour. Without a coloured stamp or signature, colour is not needed.
  • After compressing, check the smallest text, because an unreadable document counts as a missing one.
  • Do not leave uploading to the last day. Enrolment systems are busiest then and errors are more likely.

A final check

  • Is each document fully in frame, with no clipped corners?
  • Does the text read without zooming?
  • Are the pages upright?
  • Is every item on the guide's list ready?
  • Are the file names clear? Something like diploma-name-surname.pdf works well.

Open the document on your own phone and read it before uploading. If you find it hard to read, the person at the other end will not manage at all.

item.title: What Is a .udf File? Read UYAP Documents as PDF
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: UDF is a proprietary format used only by Turkey's court system, so Word, Preview and every PDF viewer ignore it. Here is how to read one in a minute.
item.content:encoded:
Someone sent you a reasoned decision or a writ from UYAP. The file ends in .udf and nothing on your computer will open it. Word does not help, and double-clicking brings up the app picker. That is not your fault: UDF is a proprietary document format used only in Turkey.

What UDF is

UDF stands for UYAP Document Format. UYAP is Turkey's National Judiciary Informatics System, run by the Ministry of Justice, and petitions, writs, procedural orders and reasoned decisions are all downloaded with this extension.

The format is built to preserve a document's integrity and the electronic signature on it. That is sound design, but in practice a document that leaves the system becomes unreadable for the other side, so the UDF you send a client will not open on their computer.

The official route and its catches

The official answer is the Ministry's free UYAP Document Editor, which opens the file and offers save as PDF. It works, but it does not suit every situation:

  • It requires an installation and may need Java on your machine.
  • Whoever you send the document to needs the same program, which is rarely realistic to expect of a client.
  • On someone else's computer, or on a phone, you cannot install anything.

The install-free route

A UDF file is really an archive carrying the document's text and formatting. That structure can be decoded and redrawn, so the file can be turned into a PDF right in the browser with nothing installed. The UDF tool on PDF Platform does this on your device, which matters because court documents carry party names, identity numbers and case details. The file is never sent to a server.

  1. Drop the file in — Drag the .udf file onto the area. You can drop several at once.
  2. Click Convert to PDF — The document is decoded in your browser, keeping fonts, bold and underlined text, alignment, tables and embedded images.
  3. Download it, or take the text — Download the PDF, or grab the plain text as a .txt file and paste it straight into Word.

UDF to PDF — Turn a .udf file from UYAP into a PDF on your own device, with nothing to install. Open the tool

The PDF is a copy, not the signed original

This distinction is worth underlining. The electronic signature in a UDF belongs to the document as it exists in that file. Convert it and you hold a readable copy, but the signature itself does not carry over.

For reading, archiving, sending to a client or consulting a colleague, the PDF is perfectly fine. For an official filing, keep using the signed UDF original.

Other common UDF problems

  • The file looks corrupt: the download may have been cut short, so download it again from UYAP.
  • The file is too large to upload: usually because of images pasted into it, which you can upload as separate exhibits.
  • It will not open on a phone: UYAP has a mobile editor app, but converting to PDF works on any device.
  • The recipient cannot open it: send a PDF, not a UDF. As a rule, any document leaving the system should be a PDF.

Editing the text in Word

There are two routes. The quick one is to copy the .txt text the tool gives you and paste it. To keep the formatting as well, convert to PDF first and then convert the PDF to Word.

item.title: Merging e-Government Documents Without Breaking Barcodes
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Merging is easy. The subtlety is that every barcoded document must stay verifiable, which rules out screenshots, rescanning and heavy compression.
item.content:encoded:
An institution wants proof of address, a civil registry extract, a criminal record certificate and a social security statement in a single file, and the portal gives you each as a separate PDF. Merging them takes a minute, but barcoded documents need one piece of care.

The barcode is the document's identity

Documents downloaded from Turkey's e-Government portal carry a barcode or QR code with a verification code. The receiving institution scans it, or types the code into the portal's verification page, to confirm the document really was issued in your name.

One rule therefore governs everything you do: the barcode must stay readable. Cropping, heavy compression or rescanning at low resolution can make it unreadable, and then the document counts as invalid.

Never print an e-government document and scan it again. The PDF you have is already digital and sharp, and printing and rescanning inflates the file and lowers the chance the barcode scans. Use the original PDF as it is.

Four steps

  1. Download each document as a PDF — Use the download as PDF option rather than screenshots, because barcodes usually do not survive a screenshot.
  2. Add them to the merge tool — Select the files in one go. Merging runs in your browser, so your documents are not uploaded.
  3. Put them in the requested order — Drag the files in the list to reorder. If an order was specified, follow it, and if not, lead with the most important document.
  4. Merge and download — Open the single PDF and check quickly that everything is there and in the right order.

Merge PDF — Put official documents in order and combine them into one file, with no signup and on your device. Open the tool

If the file is too large

Official portal documents are usually small, and together they rarely pass a few megabytes. An unexpectedly large file almost always means a scanned document slipped in, such as a photocopied diploma or a scan of an ID card.

Shrink only that scanned document, then merge. That way you never touch the sharpness of the portal's own output.

Personal data: think before you share

Official documents carry identity numbers, addresses and dates of birth. If the document goes to a government body, those details are required and should not be hidden.
