If it goes to an estate agent, a prospective employer or a website, the situation differs, and covering the fields the recipient does not need is a reasonable precaution.

Do not redact by drawing a black box over the text. A box drawn on a PDF is only a picture, and the text beneath it stays selectable and copyable. Use a tool that truly removes the data.

A final check

  • Is every document inside the file? Compare the page count against what you downloaded.
  • Do the barcodes look sharp? Zoom in and check.
  • Have any documents expired? Institutions usually want recent criminal record and address certificates.
  • Is the file name clear? Something like application-documents-name-surname.pdf helps the reader.

item.title: Sejda Alternative: Free PDF Tools With No Hourly Limit
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Sejda's free plan lets you run three tasks an hour. That is fine for one file and painful for twenty. Here is the arithmetic, the fair trade-offs, and the jobs that never needed a cap.
item.content:encoded:
Sejda is a solid PDF editor, and plenty of people use its free tier happily. The trouble starts when a job has more than three steps in it: merge a batch, split a scan, rotate the odd pages, and the clock stops you. This guide lays out exactly what the limits are, what you can do about them, and when paying Sejda is the better call.

The free limits at a glance

  • Three tasks per hour; the fourth waits for the window to reset.
  • Per-tool page caps: 50 pages for organising pages, 200 for most other tools.
  • File size caps: 50 MB for most tools, 100 MB for compression.
  • No account needed, which is a real advantage over many competitors.

Paid plans: a $5 week pass, $7.50 per user per month, or $63 a year with the desktop app included. Paid lifts the hourly and page limits and raises the file size ceiling to 500 MB.

What three an hour means in practice

Take a small accounting job: ten supplier invoices to merge into one file, then split into two, then rotate a few scanned pages. That is a dozen or more tasks. At three an hour, and assuming the window resets on the hour, you would spend roughly three to four hours finishing something that takes five minutes of actual work.

None of this is a flaw in Sejda. Anything that processes files on a server costs money per task and has to be metered somewhere. The more useful question is whether the task needed a server in the first place.

Where Sejda is the better choice

  • You need a desktop application for offline work. Sejda has one; we do not.
  • You have one big job a year. The $5 week pass beats any subscription, and we have nothing like it.
  • You want a long-established editor for changing existing text inside a PDF. Sejda has done this for years.

Which jobs never needed a server

Merging, splitting, rotating, cropping, deleting and reordering pages only rearrange what is already inside the file. A modern browser can do that locally, so the file never leaves your device and there is no per-task cost to the provider, which means nothing to count.

On PDF Platform these page tools run in your browser, with no hourly cap, no daily cap and no account, up to 80 MB per file.

Test the claim yourself: open the merge tool, switch your Wi-Fi off, and run a merge. If it completes, the work happened on your own machine.

Where we have limits too

Conversion to Word, OCR and compression run on our servers, so the free plan has a daily allowance for them. The difference from Sejda is only where the limit falls: page operations, the jobs free users run most often, are never counted here.

Merge PDF — No hourly cap, no account. It runs in your browser and your file is not uploaded. Open the tool

Quick decision guide

  • Batch page work (merge, split, rotate, delete, reorder): use a browser-based tool with no meter.
  • Editing text inside a PDF: both can do it, so compare on the file you actually have.
  • One heavy job, once: Sejda's week pass is likely cheapest.
  • Desktop software: Sejda.
  • Steady monthly volume: compare $7.50 for Sejda Web with $6.99 for PDF Platform Plus.

Neither option wins everywhere. Pick the one that matches the job in front of you.

item.title: Microsoft Lens Alternative: Scan on Your Phone
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Lens is gone and Microsoft suggests OneDrive. If you would rather not put every scanned page in a cloud, there are other routes, starting with what your phone already has.
item.content:encoded:
Microsoft Lens, formerly Office Lens, stopped creating new scans on 9 March 2026, a month after it left the app stores. If it is still installed you can open old scans but not make new ones, and a habit many people had for a decade ended quietly.

The timeline

  • 9 January 2026: retirement announced and support ended.
  • 9 February 2026: removed from the App Store and Google Play.
  • 9 March 2026: new scans stopped working.

Microsoft's suggested replacement is the scanning feature in the OneDrive app.

Why OneDrive is not for everyone

It works, but it needs a Microsoft account and sends every scan to the cloud. That is fine for a receipt. For an ID, a medical report, a tenancy agreement or a client's paperwork, it is a different decision.

There is also a simpler complaint: signing in to a cloud service just to photograph a sheet of paper is a bigger answer than the problem needs. Lens was liked because it was small. Open, shoot, PDF.

Check what your phone already does

  • iPhone: in Notes, start a new note, tap the camera icon and choose Scan Documents. It detects edges, corrects perspective and works entirely on the device.
  • Android: in Google Drive, tap the plus button and choose Scan. The result is uploaded to Drive.
  • Many Samsung phones offer to scan from the camera app when you point it at a document.

For the occasional single page, these are plenty and you need to install nothing. You can stop reading here.

Where built-in scanners run out

They tend to struggle in predictable places: joining several pages neatly, sharing the result as a PDF, making the text searchable, and repeating the job from a computer. Some workplaces also forbid installing apps on phones.

A scanner that runs in the browser fits those gaps: nothing to install, no account, and the document never leaves the device.

The PDF Platform document scanner

It opens in your phone's browser. Point the camera at a document and the edges are found automatically, an angled shot is flattened, contrast is lifted and a PDF is produced. The camera frame, the edge detection and the PDF generation all run on your device, so the document is not sent anywhere.

  • Free: camera scanning, automatic edge detection, perspective correction, contrast improvement, 3 pages per scan and PDF download. No account needed.
  • Pro: unlimited pages, automatic capture (it takes the shot when you hold the phone steady), shadow removal and searchable PDF (OCR).

Document Scanner — Open it in your phone's browser and point the camera. No install, no account. Open the tool

Three steps

  1. Open it in your phone browser — Nothing to download. Open the page, tap Scan document and allow camera access.
  2. Point at the document — Edges are found automatically, and shooting from an angle is fine because the result is flattened.
  3. Download the PDF — Several pages join into one PDF, and you can share it straight from the phone.

What you give up

  • No sync between devices. Scans do not pile up in a cloud; you save or share the PDF yourself.
  • It is not a store-installed app. You can add the site to your home screen and use it like one.
  • You need a connection the first time. Afterwards the scanning works offline, because the work was always on your device.

If you want scans collected in a cloud, Microsoft's OneDrive suggestion is the right call. If you want documents to stay on your phone, this is.

item.title: PDF24 on Mac or Linux: Private Alternatives
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: PDF24 Creator keeps your files on your computer, but only if that computer runs Windows. On Mac or Linux the online tools are the only option, and they upload.
item.content:encoded:
PDF24 has been a free, capable toolkit for years. What is easy to miss is that it is two products, and the one you can use depends on your operating system. That split explains most of the searches from Mac and Linux users.

Two products, two privacy models

  • PDF24 Tools is the online version. It works in the browser on Windows, Mac, Linux and phones, is free, needs no account and has no restrictions. Your files are uploaded to PDF24's servers to be processed; in their words, 'all files are completely removed from our servers after a short time'.
  • PDF24 Creator is the installed version. It provides the same tools offline, so nothing is uploaded. It exists for Windows only.

PDF24's own site advises installing Creator if you prefer to work offline. That advice only helps Windows users.

What this means on other systems

On Mac, Linux and Android there is no Creator, so the online tools are what is left, and they are the upload route. The option a Windows user has, keeping the document on their own machine, is simply not available.

For a receipt this hardly matters. For a contract, an ID copy, a medical report or a client's paperwork it does, and the laptop you chose should not decide how private your documents are.

Where PDF24 is strong

  • The online tools are completely free, need no account and have no daily cap.
  • On Windows, Creator is a proper desktop application that works offline and integrates with the system.
  • It is a mature, broad toolkit that has been around for years.

If you are on Windows and do not mind installing Creator, you may not need an alternative at all.

Closing the gap on any system

PDF Platform runs in the browser, so Mac, Linux, Windows and phones behave the same, and the page operations happen on your device so nothing is uploaded.

  • On your device, nothing uploaded: merge, split, rotate, crop, delete and reorder pages, image-to-PDF, signing and annotation.
  • On a server: Word, Excel and PowerPoint conversion, OCR, compression and the AI tools. A browser cannot do these alone, and each tool's page says which kind it is.

Check it in thirty seconds: open the merge tool, disconnect from the internet and run the merge. If it completes, your file is going nowhere.

What is free

PDF24's unlimited free online tools are a serious advantage, so here is the equivalent picture for us:

  • The on-device tools are free and unlimited with no account, up to 80 MB per file, and add no watermark to the output.
  • Server-side tools such as conversion and OCR have a small daily allowance on the free plan, with more on paid plans.

For page editing the free side is unlimited here too. For conversion and OCR it is not, so choose with that in mind.

Merge PDF — Mac, Linux or Windows. It runs in your browser and your file is not uploaded. Open the tool

A quick way to decide

  • On Windows and happy to install software: PDF24 Creator already works offline, so stay where you are.
  • On Mac, Linux or Android with a sensitive document: use a browser-based tool that does not upload.
  • Conversion or OCR: both send the file to a server, so the question is whose server you trust. If you want unlimited free use, PDF24 is strong.
  • A locked-down work computer where nothing can be installed: a browser-based tool is your only choice anyway.

item.title: DocuSign Alternatives for Small Teams, No Envelope Limits
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: DocuSign built the category, but it bills per envelope. If you send ten contracts a month the personal plan is spent by mid-month. Here are the numbers and the trade-offs.
item.content:encoded:
For e-signatures, DocuSign is the benchmark, and it earned that. The catch is the billing unit: you pay by the number of documents sent, and the personal plan allows five a month. A one-person business sending ten contracts runs out around the middle of the month.

The pricing, from DocuSign's own page

DocuSign counts envelopes, meaning each package of documents sent for signature.

  • Personal: $11 per month (billed annually), 5 envelopes per month.
  • Standard: $30 per user per month, 100 envelopes per user per year.
  • Business Pro: $45 per user per month, 100 envelopes per user per year.

Note that even the higher plans stop at 100 envelopes a year, roughly eight a month. Past that, you are talking to sales.

What you give up by leaving DocuSign

  • Ready-made integrations with Salesforce, SAP, Google Workspace and others.
  • Qualified electronic signature options and certifications for regulated industries.
  • Bulk send, template management, in-person signing and other advanced flows.
  • iOS and Android apps and enterprise user management.

If you need any of these, switching saves nothing. The rest of this article is for people who do not.

The job most people are actually doing

For freelancers, small agencies, accountants, estate agents and sole traders the task is usually one sentence: send this contract, let the other party sign it, and keep a record that they did. Envelope quotas, integration catalogues and user management are not part of that sentence.

How a signature request works here

  1. Upload and address — Upload the document and enter the signer's email address.
  2. The signer opens their own link — Without creating an account they view the document, type their name, draw their signature and tick the consent box.
  3. You receive the signed original — The signature is applied to the original held on the server, and a certificate is appended.

The detail worth knowing: no file ever comes back from the signer. Whether the signed document is the one you sent is settled by how the system works, not by an audit after the event.

The appended certificate records:

  • When the request was created, sent, viewed and signed.
  • The signer's name and email address and the authentication method.
  • The moment consent was given.
  • SHA-256 fingerprints of the document before and after signing.

The link is valid for 14 days. A signer can decline, optionally giving a reason; you are told by email and it goes into the audit record.

Legal validity, stated plainly

This creates a visual electronic signature with the record of the process attached, the approach used for most commercial documents. A qualified electronic signature is a separate legal category that requires a certificate from a qualified trust service provider, and we do not offer one.

If the document needs notarisation, goes to a public authority, or the law specifically demands a qualified signature, this is the wrong tool. Use DocuSign's qualified options or a local trust service provider.

Cost side by side

  • DocuSign Personal: $11 per month for 5 documents a month.
  • PDF Platform Plus: $6.99 per month with 600 operations a month and all tools. Signature requests are included from Plus upwards.

The two are not the same kind of product. DocuSign is a signing workflow; this is a document toolkit that includes signature requests. If signing is all you need, the second costs less. If you need signing infrastructure, the first gives you more.

Request a Signature — Upload the document and enter an email address. They sign without an account and the audit certificate is attached. Open the tool

Matching the tool to the situation

  • A few contracts a month with a record of the process: signature requests are enough, and cheaper.
  • A qualified signature or an industry certification: DocuSign or a local trust service provider.
  • CRM integration, bulk send or templates: DocuSign.
  • Only signing your own document: neither. The PDF signing tool is free, needs no account and runs on your device.

item.title: Why PDF Screenshots Blur, and How to Snip Sharply
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: A screenshot is limited to your screen. A snip is drawn from the document at the resolution you choose, so charts and tables stay crisp on a slide or in print.
item.content:encoded:
There is a table, chart, diagram or single question in a PDF, and you want it in a slide, a report or a lesson. The first instinct is a screenshot, and the result is usually a soft, crookedly cropped image. The better way is to cut the region straight out of the document at a resolution you choose.

Why a screenshot falls short

A screenshot copies your screen, so the image is limited to your screen's resolution rather than the PDF's.

  • Text and thin lines go soft and fall apart when you zoom in.
  • The difference shows immediately on a projector or in print.
  • Cropping the edges by hand is fiddly, with a pixel too much here and too little there.
  • Even zooming into the PDF first will not give you more than your screen has.

What a snip does instead

A snip is generated from the document, not from your screen. You select an area on the page and the tool redraws only that region at the resolution you picked. A table that looks small on screen can still become a print-quality image.

The resolution options are 1x, 2x and 3x. 1x is for screen use, 2x is plenty for print and slides, and 3x is for large output or blowing up a very small detail.

Six steps

  1. Add your PDF — Drop in your document. It never leaves your device.
  2. Pick the page — Use the page strip on the left to move to the page you want.
  3. Select the area — Drag a box on the page, then move it around and resize it from the corners.
  4. Set resolution and format — Choose 1x, 2x or 3x and PNG or JPEG. PNG suits text and graphics, and JPEG suits photos.
  5. Add the snip — It drops into the basket. Take as many snips as you like, from any page.
  6. Download — Save snips one by one, grab them all as a ZIP, or turn them into a print-ready A4 worksheet.

Snip PDF to Image — Upload a PDF and take the table, chart or question out as a sharp image. Open the tool

The snip basket

One snip is rarely enough: three charts from a report, five questions from a book. Every snip you take collects in the basket, and the page strip shows a badge with how many you took from each page. When you finish, download the lot in one go instead of handling files one at a time. The worksheet option lays your snips out on A4 pages in order, in one or two columns, ready to print. Reorder them in the basket and the sheet follows that order.

Where it helps

  • Moving a chart from a report into a slide deck.
  • Pulling one product shot out of a catalogue.
  • Collecting specific questions from lesson notes or a question bank.
  • Sharing a clause from a contract legibly instead of as a soft screenshot.
  • Lifting a logo or stamp cleanly out of an old document.

Snip, convert a page or extract images?

These are three different jobs, and knowing which one you want gets you the right result first time:

  • Snipping turns the region you choose into an image. A table, chart or paragraph, with you drawing the boundary.
  • PDF to image converts the whole page into a single image.
  • Extracting embedded images pulls out the original photo files stored inside the document. It does not capture page text or vector drawings.

PDF to Image — Download whole pages as high-resolution JPG or PNG. Open the tool

Privacy and memory

Snipping runs entirely in your browser and your PDF is never uploaded. The whole page is not drawn at a huge scale either, since only the region you selected is rendered, which keeps it fast and easy on your device's memory.

item.title: Social Media Image Sizes for 2026, Hit Them Exactly
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Upload an image at the wrong size and the platform decides how to crop it. Resize first, and you decide the framing and the sharpness yourself.
item.content:encoded:
You upload an image and it comes out cropped, cut off at the edges or soft. The cause is almost always the same: the pixel size does not match what the platform expects. Below are the sizes each network wants and a way to resize without losing quality.

Why the size matters

Social networks automatically crop and rescale whatever you upload to fit their frames. That automatic step is out of your hands, so text can end up outside the frame, faces can be cut off and an oversized file can be compressed so hard that detail falls apart. Resize before you upload and you control both the framing and the sharpness.

Sizes for 2026

  • Instagram post (square): 1080 x 1080 px.
  • Instagram post (portrait, 4:5): 1080 x 1350 px, the tallest ratio the feed allows.
  • Instagram story and Reels: 1080 x 1920 px (9:16).
  • Facebook shared image: 1200 x 630 px.
  • Facebook cover photo: 851 x 315 px.
  • X (Twitter) in-stream image: 1600 x 900 px. Header: 1500 x 500 px.
  • LinkedIn post (square): 1200 x 1200 px. Company cover: 1128 x 191 px.
  • YouTube thumbnail: 1280 x 720 px. Channel banner: 2560 x 1440 px.
  • Link preview image (OG image): 1200 x 630 px.

Publishing one image across several platforms? Start from 1080 x 1350 (4:5), which crops cleanly to both square and 9:16.

When the ratio does not match: Fill, Fit or Stretch

  • Fill (crop): fills the size exactly and crops overflowing edges from the centre. The natural choice for photos.
  • Fit (add padding): keeps the whole image visible and fills the gaps with a colour you choose. Best for product shots, logos and posters where nothing may be cut.
  • Stretch: pulls the image to the exact size and ignores the ratio. Avoid it for faces and text, because everything looks squashed.

How sharpness is preserved

Resizing is really resampling, and the filter decides the result. A browser's built-in scaling is fast but crude, so thin lines get jagged and text goes soft. The Resize Image tool uses the mks2013 filter from the Lanczos family, which scales and sharpens in one pass so fine detail survives.

  • The larger your source, the better the downscale, so crop first and then resize.
  • Enlarging cannot create detail. Blowing a 600 px wide image up to 1920 px will not sharpen it, and the tool warns you when that happens.
  • Use JPEG or WebP for photos, and PNG or WebP for logos that need transparency. WebP usually gives the smallest file at the same quality.

Resize in four steps

  1. Add your image — Drop in a JPG, PNG or WebP file. It never leaves your device.
  2. Choose the size — Pick a ready-made social size or type a width and height yourself. With Keep aspect ratio on, one side is enough.
  3. Pick how it fits — Fill, Fit or Stretch. In Fit mode you can also choose the padding colour.
  4. Resize and download — Set the format and quality, click Resize, and the result downloads instantly.

Resize Image — Upload an image and get it at exactly the pixel size you need, sharp. Open the tool

Resizing is not compressing

These are two different jobs that often get mixed up. Resizing changes the pixel dimensions of an image, such as 1920 x 1080. Compressing keeps the dimensions and reduces the file size in MB. Getting the dimensions right usually cuts the file size a lot on its own, and if it is still too big, run it through the compressor next.

Compress Image — Keep the dimensions, shrink the file size. Open the tool

Privacy

Resizing runs entirely in your browser. Your image is never uploaded and never reaches the internet, because the work happens on your computer or phone.

item.title: How to Save Original Images From a PDF
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Converting a page to a picture and pulling out the pictures inside it are two different operations with very different results. Here is when to use which.
item.content:encoded:
A PDF has a photo or logo you want as its own file. A screenshot gives you a soft, screen-sized copy. The better route is to take out the image exactly as it was embedded, at its original resolution.

Two jobs people mix up

  • PDF to image takes a picture of the whole page as JPG or PNG. Text, lines and photos are flattened together into one image.
  • Extract images does not render the page. It pulls out the embedded image files themselves, in their original format and resolution.

Need the whole page as a picture? Use PDF to Image. Need just the photos or logos at original quality? Use Extract Images.

Option 1: screenshot

It is the best-known method and the weakest. The result is capped by your screen resolution, edges are hard to crop cleanly and the original quality is gone.

Option 2: convert the page

If the picture fills the page, a high-resolution page conversion can work. If the page also holds text and other elements, everything merges into one image and you cannot isolate the photo.

PDF to Image — Download whole pages as high-resolution JPG or PNG. Open the tool

Option 3: extract the embedded images

This returns the real image streams from inside the PDF, which is what the Extract Images tool does:

  1. Upload the PDF — Choose a document that contains photos or logos. If it is encrypted, enter its password.
  2. Click Extract Images — Each page is scanned and every embedded image is pulled out in its original format (JPG or PNG). An image used on several pages is saved once.
  3. Download the ZIP — All extracted images arrive in one ZIP archive, in a single click.

Extract Images from PDF — Upload a PDF and get every photo and logo inside it, without quality loss. Open the tool

Typical uses

  • Reusing photos from a presentation or report.
  • Recovering a company logo from an old PDF at original quality.
  • Bulk-saving product images from a catalogue or brochure.

Privacy

Extraction runs on a server, but your file is not stored permanently and temporary data is cleared when the job finishes. Most of our other tools, such as merge, rotate and delete pages, run entirely in your browser.

item.title: Choosing a Free PDF Tool: Six Checks Before You Upload
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Free tools pay their bills somewhere. Six checks show where, and a thirty-second test shows whether your file is uploaded.
item.content:encoded:
Searching for a free online PDF tool returns hundreds of results, and they are not the same. Some upload your file, some add a watermark, and some ask you to sign up for a simple task. This checklist shows what to look at before you pick one.

The hidden part: uploading

In most online PDF tools, merging, splitting or converting uploads your file to their server, processes it there and then deletes it. That is usually safe, but for a contract, ID or financial statement, sending the file over the internet, even briefly, leaves a question mark. The alternative is for the operation to run directly in your browser so the file never leaves your device.

Six checks

  1. Privacy: is the file uploaded to a server, or processed in your browser? On-device is safest for sensitive documents.
  2. Forced watermark: is a stamp added to the free output? That is annoying on a professional document.
  3. Sign-up requirement: does a simple merge need an account?
  4. Usage limit: are you asked to wait or pay after a set number of free tasks?
  5. Installation: does it run in the browser, or need a program or plugin?
  6. Coverage: just merging, or also split, crop, rotate, convert and sign, whichever you will actually need?

Why on-device matters

If a tool runs the operation in your browser you gain three things: privacy, because the file does not go online; speed, because there is no upload or download wait; and offline use, since once the page has loaded it works even if your connection drops. On PDF Platform, structural tools such as merge, split, crop, rotate, delete pages, reorder and image to PDF run entirely on your device.

Try the PDF Tools — Merge, split, crop and rotate without your file leaving your device, with no sign-up, free. Open the tool

What can run locally and what cannot

Not everything can run in a browser, and the right tool is the one that tells you the split clearly. The general rule:

  • Can run on your device, file never leaves: merge, split, rotate, delete pages, reorder, crop, image to PDF, sign and annotate.
  • Needs a server: Word, Excel and PowerPoint conversion, OCR (turning scans into text), high-ratio compression and AI (summarize, chat, translate). Even here, a good tool does not store content and uses an encrypted connection.

Putting it together

  1. Is it a sensitive document? — If yes, pick a tool that runs the operation on your device so the file does not go online.
  2. Is it a simple task such as merge, split or crop? — Skip tools that require sign-up or installation. These jobs can be done instantly with no account.
  3. Do you need conversion or OCR? — Those need a server, so confirm content is not stored and an encrypted connection is used.

A quick test: open the tool, pick a file and watch how fast it finishes. If you get an instant result with no upload bar, the operation is probably running on your device. To be sure, switch off your connection and try again.

item.title: PDF Too Large for Gmail or WhatsApp? Get It Under the Limit
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: A 25 MB file often fails a 25 MB limit. Learn the real numbers, compress once and well, and know the alternatives when compression is not enough.
item.content:encoded:
You want to email a PDF but it says the file is too large, or WhatsApp will not take the document. The usual fix is not splitting it. It is compressing it: reduce the size and keep the content.

Why it is big, and the usual limits

  • Scanned documents and image-heavy PDFs take the most space.
  • Gmail attachment: about 25 MB. Outlook: about 20 MB. WhatsApp document: about 100 MB, though very large files stall in practice.
  • Portals and application systems often cap at 2 to 10 MB.

Know the real limit

Whether a file is too large depends on where you are sending it, and most people learn the limit only after hitting it. Email attachments also grow by roughly a third when encoded, so a 25 MB file often will not pass a 25 MB limit. Aim a little under the limit.

Three steps

  1. Upload the PDF — Drag and drop your file into the compress tool.
  2. Pick a compression level — At a balanced level there is no noticeable quality loss, and a higher level reduces size further.
  3. Download and send — The optimized file is now under the email or WhatsApp limit.

Compress PDF — Upload your file, compress it and download it ready to send, free. Open the tool

Does compressing hurt quality?

At a balanced level, no. Text stays selectable and crisp and images stay readable. The text layer is preserved, so you can still search and copy in the compressed PDF. The biggest savings usually come from scanned, image-heavy PDFs.

When compression is not enough

  • Delete unnecessary pages, especially blank reverse sides in scans.
  • Send only the relevant page range; enough for the recipient to do their job is enough.
  • Split the document into sensible parts and send two messages.
  • For very large files, a cloud link is more reliable than an attachment.

If you are sending several documents as one file, compress first, then combine them with Merge PDF.

WhatsApp specifics

WhatsApp does not compress documents and sends them as they are, which is good because the document is not degraded. If you send a photo as an image, however, the app shrinks it and paperwork can become unreadable. For documents, convert the photo to PDF and send it as a document, which preserves quality and looks more professional.

Check the result

The effect of compression is invisible at normal screen scale. After downloading, open the page with the smallest type and zoom in. If the letters read cleanly, the file is usable. Do not skip this on documents going to an institution, because an illegible scan is one of the most common reasons applications come back.

Do it once

Compressing the same document a second and third time costs a little more quality each round without meaningful size gains. Reach the target in one pass. If you cannot, the problem is the content rather than the compression, and with many high-resolution scans, splitting or removing pages is the real solution.

Keep it small from the start

  • Scan text documents at 300 DPI, because 600 DPI inflates the file for no benefit.
  • Scan black-and-white paperwork in greyscale rather than colour.
  • Run phone photos through the Document Scanner instead of converting straight to PDF.
  • Review the page count before sharing, since that is where the easiest gains are.

item.title: Edit and Sign a PDF on Your Phone, No App Needed
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Signing is something phones do better than computers. Here is what to do on a small screen, and what to leave for a bigger one.
item.content:encoded:
You need to sign a document or add a note to a form while out, and you do not want to install a PDF app. You do not have to. Most of this works in your phone's browser with no installation.

What you can do with no app

  • Add text and notes and fill in blanks: the Annotate tool.
  • Sign by drawing with your finger, typing, or uploading a photo: the Sign tool.
  • Highlight, draw boxes and sketch: the Annotate tool.
  • Actually delete and change existing text: the Edit tool.

Three steps on Android or iPhone

  1. Open the tool in your browser — Open the tool page in your phone browser, Chrome or Safari, with nothing to install.
  2. Upload your PDF — Pick your file, and the annotate and sign tools run right on the phone.
  3. Edit and download — Sign or mark with your finger, then save with Apply and download.

Annotate PDF on Your Phone — Add text, sign and annotate on your phone with no app, for free. Open the tool

What is comfortable on a phone

A small screen makes some jobs easier and others harder. Setting expectations first saves you from struggling on a phone and then reaching for a computer anyway.

  • Comfortable: deleting, reordering, rotating and merging pages, because you touch large targets.
  • Comfortable: signing, since a signature drawn with a finger usually beats one drawn with a mouse.
  • Moderate: adding text notes, where placement needs zooming in.
  • Hard: filling forms with many fields and anything needing precise alignment.
  • Hard: processing scans of hundreds of pages, where memory can run short.

Preparing a signature

A signature drawn with a finger or stylus looks far more natural than one drawn with a mouse, and holding the phone in landscape and zooming in gives a steadier line. Alternatively, sign once on white paper and upload the photo, and the tool cleans the background and places it on the document.

After filling and signing, you can email or WhatsApp the file straight from your phone.

Files in and out

The real difficulty on a phone is file traffic rather than the operation. An email attachment usually has to be saved first, and documents from messaging apps land in their own folders. When the work finishes the result goes to downloads and can be sent straight to email or a messaging app from the share menu. Once you learn that flow, the next document takes a few taps.

The typical phone problem: a skewed photo

Most paperwork photographed with a phone comes out slightly skewed and shadowed. Converting those straight to PDF produces something the recipient cannot read and that official applications may reject. The document scanning flow finds the edges and corrects perspective, so the same photo gives a far more acceptable document.

Is my file safe?

Annotating and signing happen entirely in your phone's browser, so the PDF is not uploaded and stays private. Only true text deletion and editing runs on a server, and the file is not stored after processing.

Screens and privacy

On a phone, documents often get opened on public transport or in an office where others can see the screen. With sensitive documents, check your surroundings and delete intermediate copies from downloads when you finish. Page operations run on the device so the document does not travel, and the remaining risk is physical.

item.title: Do You Need Adobe Acrobat? A Free Browser Alternative
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Acrobat is excellent software for specialist work. Most everyday PDF jobs are far simpler. Here is how to tell which group you are in.
item.content:encoded:
Adobe Acrobat is powerful, but the full version is paid and needs installing. For most everyday PDF tasks you need neither a subscription nor an install, and you can do it all free in your browser. The test is what you actually do.

Where Acrobat is genuinely strong

Acrobat has been the industry standard for a long time, for good reasons. For building complex forms, working with pre-press colour and trim settings, certificate-based digital signatures, accessibility tags and large corporate workflows, it has few rivals. If you do that work regularly, the subscription earns its keep.

But is that what most people do?

In practice most PDF work is far simpler: merging a few files, deleting pages, fixing a sideways page, shrinking a document, signing a form and occasionally converting to Word. A full desktop suite and a monthly fee are well beyond that. Ask yourself how many of the things you did in Acrobat last month actually required Acrobat.

What you can do without it

  • Merge, split, rotate, delete pages and reorder pages, free and on your device.
  • Image to PDF, document scanning, page numbers and watermarks.
  • Adding text, annotating and signing.
  • Word, Excel and PowerPoint conversion, compression and OCR, on the server with content not stored.

PDF Platform runs entirely in the browser, so there is no download, install or plugin. Structural tasks such as merge, split and sign happen on your device and the file does not even go to a server. An account is only needed for larger files, history and advanced conversion.

Open PDF Tools — Merge, convert and sign with no install, free. Open the tool

Do not install Acrobat just to sign or merge one PDF. You can do it in the browser in seconds, without your file leaving your device.

What working without an install buys you

  • You can work on locked-down work computers without admin rights.
  • Mac, Linux, Chromebook and phone all behave the same.
  • There are no version updates, licence renewals or installation problems.
  • On someone else's computer you get the job done without touching your account.
  • Because page operations run locally, files do not leave the corporate network.

Reader is not Acrobat

Acrobat Reader is free, but it is a reader. It displays documents, adds comments and fills forms. Deleting pages, merging, converting and editing belong to the paid version. That distinction surprises many people and answers the common question of why Acrobat will not delete a page. Browser-based tools fill exactly that gap.

Checks before you switch

Three things matter when moving to an alternative: does it cover everything you actually do, is the output quality what you expect, and where do your documents go? The first two become clear after trying a few files. The third has a simple test. Run the operation with your connection off, and if it completes, the file never left your device.

item.title: How to Crop a PDF: Select an Area, Save It as PDF or Image
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Most of the time you do not need to shrink a page. You need one table, one question or one signature box out of it. Here is how to cut exactly that out, and how it differs from trimming the page box.
item.content:encoded:
When people search for how to crop a PDF, they usually want one of two things: to cut away white margins, or to pull one specific part out of a page. Both come down to the same move. You draw a box over what you want to keep and save only that. Everything runs in your browser, so the file stays on your device.

Where cropping a PDF is useful

  • Sharing one table or chart without the rest of the page.
  • Pulling a single question out of an exam paper.
  • Sending only the relevant part of a receipt or invoice.
  • Leaving the wide empty borders of a scan out of the result.

Step by step

  1. Open the PDF — Drop it into the Snip PDF tool. The first page appears on screen and you can move between pages.
  2. Draw the box — Drag across the page. You can move the box and resize it from its corners, and zoom the window to fine-tune the edges.
  3. Click Add snip — The area goes into a list. Add more from this or other pages and reorder them in the list.
  4. Pick a format and download — Save as PDF, PNG or JPEG. Choose 2x or 3x resolution if it will be printed.

Snip PDF to Image — Select the area you want and save it as a PDF or an image, on your device, free. Open the tool

Three ways to save the PDF

  • All one after another: snips are placed on A4 pages in order, in one or two columns. Two columns suit narrow snips and save paper. The result is a printable worksheet.
  • One snip per page: a single PDF where each snip sits on its own page at its own size.
  • Each snip as a separate PDF file: every snip becomes its own PDF. With more than one they arrive together in a ZIP; a single snip downloads as a plain PDF. This is the one to pick when each piece goes to a different person.

Snipping versus trimming the page box

Some programs crop by shrinking the page's CropBox. The trimmed part stays inside the file and is only hidden, so text in it can still be found and copied. Snipping works differently: the selected area is drawn as an image and only that area reaches the output. What you left out never makes it into the file.

That cuts both ways. It is reassuring when you share part of a document. The trade-off is that the snip is a picture, so its text cannot be selected or searched. If you need the text, run the result through Searchable PDF afterwards.

Resolution and file size

Higher resolution gives a sharper snip and a bigger file. 2x is enough for most jobs and prints cleanly. 3x helps with fine print in tables. 1x is only for something viewed on a screen. If the file grows too large to email, compress the result with Compress PDF.

On a phone

It works in a phone browser with nothing to install. Drag with a finger and adjust from the corners, and zoom in when you need a precise edge.

item.title: Sending Your CV as a PDF: Format, Name and ATS Checks
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Your CV is often read by software before a person sees it. A PDF with real text, a clean layout and a sensible name gets through that first step.
item.content:encoded:
A CV is the first document an employer sees about you, and a résumé built in Word can shift on other computers or change its fonts. The fix is simple: convert it to PDF before sending. The details below decide whether it is also read correctly by the software many employers use.

Why PDF

  • It looks the same on every device, with fonts, line spacing and layout preserved whoever opens it.
  • It is the professional standard, and most employers and career portals prefer or even require it.
  • It will not change by accident, whereas a Word file can shift when opened.

Convert in three steps

  1. Upload your Word file — Drag your .doc or .docx résumé into the Word to PDF tool.
  2. Convert — The PDF is prepared instantly with fonts, tables and layout preserved.
  3. Download and name it — Save the PDF with a clean name such as First_Last_CV.pdf.

Convert Word to PDF — Upload your résumé and download it as a PDF without breaking the formatting, for free. Open the tool

How application systems read your CV

At many large employers and career portals your CV is read by software first, and reaching a person depends on that. These systems parse the text in the document, so your PDF must contain real text. A CV exported as an image from a design tool, or built from a screenshot, is a blank page to the system. Test it by opening the PDF and trying to select your name with the cursor. If you cannot, it is an image.

Layouts that make automatic reading harder

  • Two-column designs, where reading order can scramble and details run together.
  • Burying information in text boxes or tables.
  • Putting contact details in the page header, since some systems never read headers.
  • Showing skill levels only as bars or stars, because information with no text equivalent is not recorded.
  • Unusual section headings; a creative title instead of Experience makes matching harder.

Clean up before converting

A PDF freezes the Word document as it stands, so turn off track changes, accept all revisions and delete comments first, or those traces can end up in the output. Check the author name in the document properties too. If you took the template from someone else, another name may still be sitting there.

File name and sending

A recruiter downloads dozens of files a day, and a document called cv_final_v3.pdf gets lost in the folder. A name in the form First_Last_CV is easier to find and looks considered. When a cover letter and certificates are requested, merging them into one PDF is tidier than separate attachments, and page numbers show the document arrived complete.

If you are asked to send several documents (CV, cover letter and certificates) as one file, convert them to PDF and then combine them with Merge PDF.

A last look before sending

  • Do fonts and alignment look the same as in Word?
  • Are links such as LinkedIn and your portfolio clickable and pointing at the right address?
  • Is the file size reasonable? Compress it if a photo inflated it.
  • Is there an old employer name or a draft note left in that you did not want shown?
  • Open it on a phone once, because many recruiters take their first look there.

item.title: Fill In a PDF Form Without Printing, Even With No Fields
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Most PDF forms you receive are flat, with nothing to click. Here is a thirty-second way to tell, and how to fill each kind cleanly.
item.content:encoded:
Applications, contracts, petitions: most PDF forms are flat, with no ready fields to click and type into. You do not need to print and fill them by hand. You can put text directly on top of the page.

Which kind of form do you have?

Open the PDF and click a blank. If a cursor blinks and you can type, the form is fillable. If nothing happens, it is flat.

  • Fillable (interactive) form: it has ready fields that you click and type into in any PDF reader. Filling the fields directly is the cleanest route because the text sits inside the field and aligns itself.
  • Flat form: most official and scanned documents are like this. There are no ready fields, so you add text on top of the page at the right spot.

Filling a flat form in three steps

  1. Upload the form — Upload your PDF form to the annotate and text tool.
  2. Add text — With the text tool, click the relevant blank and type your answer. Add a separate box for each field.
  3. Sign and download — If needed, add your signature and download the filled PDF with Apply and download.

Add Text and Markup to PDF — Upload your form, add text to the blanks and download the filled PDF for free. Open the tool

For checkboxes, add a small X or tick as text. If the form has several pages, add text and marks to each page separately.

Alignment on flat forms

  • Set the text size close to the line height; oversized text spills onto the neighbouring line.
  • Use a separate text box for each field, because one long line breaks the alignment.
  • A small mark is enough for a checkbox, so do not overflow the box.
  • Where day, month and year have separate boxes, type into each one separately.
  • Check at 100% zoom before downloading, since text that looks right at screen scale can shift in print.

Accented characters in fillable forms

Some PDF forms are built with a limited character set, so letters outside it can disappear or turn into question marks when typed. That is the form author's font choice, not a mistake by whoever fills it in. Reading the fields back once after filling is the practical way to catch it.

Why lock a fillable form

A fillable form sent as it is stays editable, so the recipient can change a field without noticing, and the form may look empty in a different program. Locking the fields makes what you typed a permanent part of the page, so the document looks the same everywhere. On an official application this ensures the form arrives complete and unaltered.

Signing and sending

If the form asks for a signature, draw or type yours after filling and place it. Signing happens entirely on your device and the document is not sent to a server. Sending one file with the signature included is tidier than separate pages. If the other side must sign too, send the document out for signature by email and keep a record of the process.

A final check

Are all required fields filled, is the date in the requested format, and are the requested attachments included? Those three questions prevent most applications from coming back. Keep a copy of the completed form too, which removes the later question of what you wrote.

item.title: iLovePDF Alternative: Free, No Watermark, Nothing Uploaded

Where the file goes

That is usually safe, but the file still travels over the internet for a while. For confidential documents the safest approach is that it never leaves your device.

What runs where

  • On the server, content not stored and connection encrypted: Word, Excel and PowerPoint conversion, OCR, compression and AI tools (summarize, chat, translate).

Which should you pick?

There is no single right answer, because it depends on what you are doing.

  • A sensitive document and page-level editing: pick the on-device tool. A file that is never uploaded beats a promise to delete it later.
  • You want a desktop program: we run in the browser, so look elsewhere.

Test the claim yourself

You do not have to take 'your file stays on your device' on trust. You can check it in thirty seconds:

  1. Open the merge tool — No account needed. Pick a couple of PDFs you want to merge.
  2. Disconnect from the internet — Turn off Wi-Fi or unplug the cable. Do not reload the page.
  3. Run the merge — It completes and you download your file. If it works with no connection, your file is not going anywhere.

item.title: SmallPDF Alternative: Why Some PDF Jobs Can Be Unlimited

item.content:encoded:
SmallPDF is a solid tool, but on the free tier you hit a daily task limit and frequent signup and Pro prompts. Can the same jobs be done with no limit and no account? For many of them, yes, and the reason says something about how these tools are built.

The free-tier limits

  • Signup and Pro pressure: some tools and batch operations require an account.
  • Upload: for most operations your file goes to a server.

Where SmallPDF is good

SmallPDF has been doing this for a long time and it shows. The interface is clean and easy to learn, the tool range is broad, there are desktop and mobile apps, and team accounts and cloud integrations help in corporate use. If you want a shared cloud workflow for a team, those features matter.

Where the real difference lies

The difference is not the feature list but where the work happens. Every server-side tool costs money to run, and that cost has to be capped somewhere, which is why daily and hourly limits exist. Page operations need no server. Done in the browser, there is nothing left to meter, so the limit disappears because the server cost disappeared, not out of generosity.

Measure your own need

item.title: Free PDF Editor Guide: Text, Notes, Signatures, Forms
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Most failed PDF edits come from using the wrong tool for the job. Four questions tell you which one you need.
item.content:encoded:
Editing a PDF means different things to different people. Some want to change existing text, some want to add notes on top, and some want to sign. With the right tool each takes seconds. Here is a roadmap by need.

Four questions first

Editing a PDF is not one job but a shared name for several similar-looking jobs with different results. The wrong tool makes the task look impossible or gives an unexpected outcome.

  • Are you changing text in the document? You need text editing.
  • Are you adding your own notes? Markup is enough.
  • Are you arranging pages by deleting, reordering or merging? Use the page tools.
  • Are you removing information permanently? Use redaction, because markup or cropping will not do.

1. Change or delete existing text

To remove text in a PDF and type new text, use the Edit PDF tool. Draw a box over the text to change, type the new text (leave it empty to delete) and download.

Edit PDF — Truly delete and replace existing text. Draw a box, type the new text and download. Open the tool

2. Add text, notes or marks on top

To add text, highlights, boxes or drawings on top without touching existing text, the Annotate PDF tool is ideal. You can also use it to fill in blanks on forms.

3. Sign

Use the Sign PDF tool to draw, type or upload your signature and place it anywhere on the page. Signing happens entirely on your device.

4. Fill forms

For flat forms with no fillable fields, add text directly on top. Our form-filling guide has the detailed steps.

For confidential documents, annotating and signing run entirely on your device and the file does not go to a server. Real text deletion and editing is done on a secure server, and the file is not stored after processing.

What to watch for in free tools

A tool offered free usually charges somewhere else, so see where before you start. The common patterns are a watermark on the output, a daily or hourly limit, your document uploaded to a server, a mandatory account before download, and reduced quality in the downloaded file. Checking those five points while trying a tool keeps you from getting stuck mid-task.

Before you start

The type of document largely decides what you can do. A PDF with a text layer lets you change the text, while in a scan the page is an image and needs converting to text first. If the document is password-protected, no tool can read its content until the password is removed. Those two checks answer most of the 'why is it not working?' questions upfront.

Common scenarios and the right order

  • Changing a clause in a scanned contract: convert to text first, then edit.
  • Turning several documents into one file: merge, then reorder, then add numbers last.
  • Cleaning a document before sharing: delete unneeded pages, redact sensitive data, clear metadata.
  • Filling and returning a form: fill, sign, lock, and compress if needed.

The limits of editing

Text in a PDF does not flow, so replacing a word with a longer one does not reflow the line. For small corrections that is no problem, but if paragraphs will be rewritten, producing the document from its source or converting to Word is less work. A few words means edit directly, and pages of rewriting means convert.

item.title: Word to PDF: A Pre-Flight Checklist So Nothing Shifts
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: A PDF freezes your Word file exactly as it stands, including track changes and old comments. A short pre-flight check keeps the result clean.
item.content:encoded:
Send a Word file and a different Office version or a missing font on the other end can shift your layout. A PDF looks identical for everyone, but it also freezes everything in the file, so it pays to clean the document before converting.

Why convert at all

  • It locks the layout, so fonts, tables and spacing look the same everywhere.
  • It opens on any device, from a phone to a computer, with no special software.
  • It cannot be edited by accident, which suits proposals, contracts and CVs.
  • Official submissions usually require a PDF.

Three steps

  1. Upload the document — Drag your .doc, .docx, .odt or .rtf file into the Word to PDF tool.
  2. Convert — The document is processed on the server and turned into a PDF with layout, fonts and tables preserved.
  3. Preview and download — Check the result and download it. The page structure matches your original.

Word to PDF — Convert your Word document to PDF with layout intact. Open the tool

If your document uses standard fonts such as Arial, Times New Roman or Calibri, the output will be closest to the original. Very custom fonts that are not installed may render differently on some systems.

Pre-flight checklist

  • Turn off track changes and accept all revisions, or the markup can end up in the output.
  • Clear comments, especially leftovers from internal review.
  • Run the spell check once, since fixing a typo in a PDF is far harder.
  • Update the automatic contents page and field codes, or old page numbers get frozen in.
  • Review the author and company details in the document properties.

Why fonts move

A Word file usually does not embed its typefaces and only records their names. If the font is missing on the other computer, the program substitutes something similar, line lengths change, tables overflow and even the page count differs. A PDF embeds the fonts it uses. That is its most useful property, and the reason official submissions ask for it.

A note for CVs and applications

Application systems often scan uploaded files automatically, so the text inside the PDF must be real text. A document produced straight from Word satisfies that, while a CV exported as an image from a design tool or captured as a screenshot does not. Test it by opening the PDF and trying to select your name with the cursor. If you cannot, it is an image.

Check the output

  • Is the page count as expected, or did an extra blank page appear?
  • Are tables split across a page break?
  • Is there an unwanted break between a heading and its text?
  • Did links stay clickable?
  • Does the file size fit the channel you are sending through?

Going the other way

Need an editable Word file back from a PDF? There is a separate tool for that.

PDF to Word — No editable version on hand? Convert the PDF back to Word. PDF to Word

Once you have the PDF you can keep working on it: merge it with annexes, add page numbers, reduce its size or permanently remove sensitive details. Most of these operate at page level and leave the content and appearance untouched.
