item.title: Excel to PDF Without Split Columns: Print Setup Tips
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: What the PDF looks like is decided by the print settings in your workbook. Two minutes of setup separates a clean quote from a scatter of columns.
item.content:encoded:
Send an Excel file as it is and columns often shift, pages split and the print area breaks on the other end. A PDF looks identical for everyone, as long as the workbook is set up properly first.

Why convert

  • It locks the layout, so cells, column widths and page breaks look the same everywhere.
  • It is print-ready, and print-area and fit-to-page problems disappear.
  • It cannot be changed by accident, which suits report, quote and invoice tables.
  • It opens on devices without Excel installed.

Three steps

  1. Upload the Excel file — Add your .xls, .xlsx, .ods or .csv file to the Excel to PDF tool.
  2. Convert — The file is processed on the server and turned into a PDF with tables, cells and formatting preserved.
  3. Preview and download — Check the result and download the PDF, ready to share and print.

Excel to PDF — Convert your Excel table to PDF with layout intact. Open the tool

Set the print options first

A wide table converted without print settings comes out with columns scattered across pages and is unreadable. A couple of minutes of setup completely changes how usable the output is.

  • Set the orientation to landscape; with many columns this is almost always needed.
  • Define the print area to stop empty cells spreading across pages.
  • Use the option to fit all columns on one page.
  • Set the header row to repeat on every page, which decides readability on multi-page tables.
  • Decide whether gridlines should print.

For wide tables with many columns, landscape orientation and an adjusted print area in Excel before converting keep everything on the page and readable.

Workbooks with several sheets

An Excel file usually holds several worksheets, and not all need sharing. If working calculations, raw data or old period tabs end up in the output, the document bloats and may carry information that was never meant to leave. Decide which sheets go into the output before converting, rather than deleting pages afterwards.

Hidden information

Excel files carry more than they show: hidden rows and columns, data concealed by filters, cell notes and other sheets that formulas point at. Hidden rows usually stay out of the PDF, but cell notes and filtered data can appear unexpectedly. Review everything hidden before converting a table that is going outside.

Quotes and invoices

The real reason to convert a quote or invoice prepared in Excel is to create a fixed document whose figures the recipient cannot change. Two extra steps help: page numbers show completeness on multi-page quotes, and a permissions password restricts copying and editing.

Before you send it

  • Do page breaks fall in sensible places, or is a line item split in half?
  • Do amounts and currency display correctly?
  • Is the smallest type readable, especially if it will be printed?
  • Is there a note or column left in that you did not want shown?

The other direction

If you have a PDF and want to edit the table inside it in Excel, a separate tool extracts tables to .xlsx.

PDF to Excel — Export tables from a PDF into editable Excel. PDF to Excel

item.title: PDF to JPG or PNG: Pick the Right Format and Resolution
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: A PDF cannot go everywhere, but an image can. Here is how to convert pages cleanly, which format to pick and the side effects to expect.
item.content:encoded:
To share a page on social media, place it on a web page or drop it into a slide, an image is far easier to use than a PDF. Converting the page to JPG or PNG is the most practical route.

Where it helps

  • Sharing a single page as an image on social media.
  • Adding a preview to a website or blog post.
  • Dropping a page into a presentation as a picture.
  • Quickly showing a page to someone who cannot open a PDF.

Three steps

  1. Upload the PDF — Add your document to the PDF to JPG tool.
  2. Pages become images — Each page is processed as a separate high-resolution JPG or PNG.
  3. Download — Take the images one by one or all together as a ZIP.

PDF to JPG — Turn PDF pages into high-quality images. Open the tool

JPG or PNG?

JPG is smaller and ideal for photo-heavy pages. PNG keeps sharp edges and crisper text and supports transparency, so prefer it for logos, diagrams and text-heavy pages.

Resolution cannot be fixed afterwards

Converting a page turns a vector document into pixels, and the resolution you choose decides the quality with no way back, because an image made at low resolution cannot be sharpened later. Roughly, medium suits on-screen sharing, high suits presentations and the web, and the highest suits print.

Why a screenshot is not enough

A screenshot looks like the fastest option, but the result is limited to your screen's resolution and usually comes out soft. It also picks up the frame, the margins and the viewer's interface. Converting directly gives a clean output at the page's own resolution, with straight edges and crisp text.

Whole page, embedded image or just a region?

This tool converts the whole page. If you only want a photo or logo inside the PDF at original quality, extract the embedded images instead of rasterizing the page, and there is no quality loss.

Extract Images from PDF — Pull embedded photos and logos out of a PDF in their original format. Open the tool

Often what you need is a table, chart or paragraph on the page rather than the page. Snipping the area directly is faster than converting and cropping in an image editor, and it preserves resolution.

Notes for social media and the web

  • A portrait A4 page is cropped in most social feeds, so snip the section you want first.
  • Compressing an image before putting it on a web page noticeably improves load time.
  • PNG works better for text-heavy pages and JPG for photo-heavy ones.
  • Text in a converted page is no longer text, so search engines cannot read it. Write important wording on the page as well.

A side effect to know about

When a page becomes an image its text layer disappears. It can no longer be copied, searched or read by screen readers. Sometimes that is what you want, but where accessibility matters or the document will be archived, keep the PDF itself and use the image only as a sharing copy.

The reverse

If you have several photos and want one PDF, a separate tool does that, and it runs entirely on your device.

Images to PDF — Combine your photos into a single PDF, on your device. Images to PDF

item.title: PDF Privacy: Which Tools Keep Your File on Your Device
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: 'We delete files after an hour' is not the same as 'we never received your file'. Here is how to tell the difference and how to handle sensitive documents.
item.content:encoded:
Most online PDF tools work the same way: your file is uploaded to their servers, processed there and handed back. For contracts, IDs and invoices that means a copy of your file lands on a server you do not control. For most structural PDF operations, that is unnecessary.

What on-device means

On-device, or client-side, processing means the whole job happens inside your browser and the file is never sent over the internet. That gives you three things: privacy, because the file stays with you; speed, because there is no upload or download wait; and the ability to work offline.

Test any tool in thirty seconds

A privacy claim means something when it can be tested. Try the operation with your connection switched off. If it completes, the file never left your device, because there was nothing to send. That test gives a more definite answer than any privacy page.

What 'deleted after an hour' really means

That is the privacy promise of most online tools, and it is an honest one, but it misses what people worry about. Until deletion the file sat on a server, crossed the network to get there and was visible to anyone with access to that system during the window. With a tool that runs on your device, no copy is ever created, so there is nothing to delete. The difference is not the quality of the policy but the fact that the file never travelled.

Tools that run in your browser

  • Merge, Split, Rotate, Delete Pages and Reorder Pages, all on your device.
  • Images to PDF, signing and annotating a PDF, on your device.
  • Document Scanner, including the camera image, entirely on your device.

Merge On-Device — Merge your PDFs in your browser, without uploading to a server. Open the tool

Does every tool run on-device?

No, and it is better to say so. Heavy jobs such as Word and Excel conversion, OCR and compression run on the server because they are not practical in a browser. With AI tools your file is not uploaded; the text is extracted on your device and only the text is processed. It should always be clear which tool runs where.

Why some jobs need a server

That not every tool runs locally is a matter of the work's nature rather than a choice. Rearranging, merging, rotating or deleting pages changes the document's structure, which a browser handles comfortably. Word conversion, OCR, compression and AI processing need serious computing power and large components, and downloading those into every visitor's browser would be neither fast nor realistic.

A practical rule for your own documents

  • Identity, medical, financial and legal documents: do everything you can on your device.
  • If a document with personal data must be processed on a server, remove what is not needed first.
  • For internal or already public documents, the distinction matters little in practice.
  • When unsure, ask whether it would trouble you if the document got out. If not, server processing is fine.

For the most sensitive documents, such as IDs, contracts and health records, prefer the on-device structural tools and the document scanner, and if needed remove sensitive data with real redaction before sharing.

Redact Sensitive Data — Permanently remove personal data before sharing. Redaction tool

Where privacy alone is not enough

A file not being uploaded does not make the document safe. When the work is done, the document sits on your device, and one left in the downloads folder of a shared computer is a bigger risk than a server ever was. After working with sensitive documents, delete intermediate copies and clear metadata before sharing.

item.title: PDF Won't Open or Looks Damaged? Diagnose, Then Repair
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Not every PDF that refuses to open is broken. Run a few quick checks first, then repair. In most damaged files the pages are still inside and only the index is wrecked.
item.content:encoded:
A 'file is damaged' or 'cannot open' error on an important PDF is maddening. The good news is that in most broken PDFs the content is still there and only the file's structure is damaged, which can often be repaired.

Check before you repair

A few minutes of checking often solves the problem, or at least reveals the real cause.

  • Try a different program: a document that opens in a browser may fail in an old desktop reader.
  • Look at the file size. A few kilobytes means the download was cut short, and re-downloading beats repairing.
  • Check the extension, because on some systems the file is actually a .zip or .docx.
  • If it asks for a password, the file is encrypted rather than broken and needs different handling.
  • If it sits in a cloud folder, check whether it has finished syncing.

Why PDFs break

  • An interrupted download or transfer, because the connection dropped.
  • A USB or disk error, or the file not being fully saved.
  • Editing with an incompatible program or a faulty export.
  • Email or attachment compression corrupting the file.

Repair in three steps

  1. Upload the broken PDF — Add the file that will not open to the Repair PDF tool.
  2. Let the repair run — The tool re-packages the file's structure and gathers the salvageable content.
  3. Download the result — Download the repaired PDF and try opening it. Much of the content may come back.

Repair PDF — Try to repair your PDF that will not open and recover the content. Open the tool

What repair actually does

At the end of a PDF sits an index recording where each object is in the file. When that index is damaged the reader cannot open the document, even though the page content is still there. Repair scans the file from start to finish, collects the objects it can find and re-packages them with a new index. That is why success is high for structural damage and low when the content itself is truly gone.

What to expect

Repair is not guaranteed, because it depends on the degree of damage. It cannot bring back fully deleted or encrypted data, but trying often recovers the document.

Check the repaired document

  • Page count: is anything missing?
  • Is the text selectable, or have pages turned into images?
  • Are the images in place, or showing as empty boxes?
  • Do bookmarks and links still work?
  • Are the last page and the signature section complete?

If the file is very large after repair, shrink it with the compress tool. If it was scanned and the text is gone, add a text layer again with OCR.

Making the recovered file usable

Repair sometimes costs the text layer and leaves pages as images, and you can add a text layer again with OCR. If the file came out larger than expected, compress it, and if some pages stayed blank or broken, delete them. Save the recovered version under a new name and do not delete the damaged original straight away, since you may want to try another approach later.

Avoiding it next time

A large share of corruption happens in transfer. Make sure a big download is not interrupted, wait for safe removal before pulling out a USB drive, and do not keep the only copy of an important document on removable media. Keeping critical documents in two separate places is the simplest and most effective precaution.

item.title: PDF Tables to Excel: Why Copy-Paste Fails
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: A PDF has no real table, only lines and aligned text. Knowing that explains the odd results, and tells you when to convert and when to extract fields instead.
item.content:encoded:
To analyze a report, price list or table from a PDF in Excel, the data first has to land in proper cells. Copy and paste usually dumps everything into one column. Here is how to export tables cleanly.

Three steps

  1. Upload the PDF — Add your document with tables to the PDF to Excel tool.
  2. Tables are extracted — The table structure on the pages is detected and written to .xlsx with rows and columns preserved.
  3. Download the Excel file — Edit, filter and calculate directly in Excel.

PDF to Excel — Export PDF tables into an editable Excel file. Open the tool

Why tables sometimes come out wrong

A PDF contains no table object. The grid you see is drawn with lines and aligned pieces of text, and no row-and-column relationship exists underneath. The conversion infers it from positions. The cases where inference is hard are predictable:

  • Tables without rules: when columns are separated only by whitespace, the boundaries blur.
  • Merged cells: a heading spanning two columns breaks the alignment.
  • Long text wrapping onto a second line makes it unclear whether it is one row or two.
  • On tables running across pages, a repeated header row can look like a new table.
  • Scanned documents need OCR first, otherwise cells come back empty.

First fixes in Excel

A few standard corrections make the output usable: format columns that did not arrive as numbers, convert amounts that became text because of thousand separators, check the date column format, delete repeated header rows and remove empty columns. Make them a habit and you will not start from scratch each time.

Convert the table, or extract fields?

Plain conversion carries the table across as it is. Often, though, you want specific fields rather than the table: the amount, date and seller on an invoice. If every document has a different layout, moving the table does not help, and you need the fields by name. A simple test: the same template with a clean grid means conversion, and differing documents with specific fields means extraction.

To gather dozens of invoices into a single CSV table, the Extract Data and Batch tools are built for exactly this, with one row per document.

Extract Data — Pull fields from complex documents such as invoices with AI. Extract with AI

Large reports

If you only need the table on page fifteen of a hundred-page report, converting the whole document is unnecessary work. Split out the relevant page range and convert only that, which is faster and leaves no surplus rows to remove.

A quick way to check the result

Rather than reading row by row, check with totals. Does the amount column sum to the document's grand total? Does the row count match the number of line items? Are there empty cells? Those three checks catch most errors in seconds.

item.title: PDF Work on Your Phone Without Installing an App
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Free PDF apps usually charge in something other than money. Most everyday jobs run in your phone's browser instead, and the file stays on your device.
item.content:encoded:
When you need to merge two PDFs or scan a document on your phone, there is no need to visit an app store for a bulky, ad-filled app. Most of these jobs run right in the phone's browser, on your device.

What runs in the browser

  • Merging and splitting PDFs.
  • Deleting, rotating and reordering pages.
  • Creating a PDF from images and photos.
  • Scanning documents with the camera, with edge detection and perspective correction.

Merge on Phone — Merge two PDFs on your phone, no app needed. Open the tool

The hidden price of free apps

Most free PDF apps are not really free. The usual pattern is predictable: watermarks on the output, a daily operation limit, your documents uploaded to the app's cloud account, broader permissions than the job needs and a subscription screen. None of that is worth accepting to merge a PDF a few times a year.

In the browser, a link opens and the job is done. Because these structural tasks run on your device, your file is not sent to the internet, so you get speed and privacy together.

Scanning with the camera

The Document Scanner uses your camera to find the document's corners, correct the perspective and produce a clean PDF, entirely on your device. You can digitize IDs, contracts or invoices without sending them to the cloud.

Scan Document — Scan a document with your phone camera into a PDF, on your device and private. Open the scanner

Getting at the file

The step people get stuck on is not the operation but finding the file. An email attachment has to be saved to the phone first, and documents from messaging apps land in their own folder. Once the file picker opens you can reach device storage and your cloud accounts. When the work is done the result lands in downloads, and sharing it from there is one tap.

The jobs people do most often

  • Turning photographed paperwork into a single PDF, by far the most common need.
  • Merging several PDFs and sending them as one file.
  • Deleting unwanted pages and fixing sideways ones.
  • Shrinking a document to fit an email.
  • Signing a form and sending it back.

Photographing paperwork

Whether photographed paperwork is accepted is usually decided at the moment of the shot. Put the document on a flat surface, light it from the front, keep all four edges in frame and hold the phone parallel to the page. If there are shadows or skew, use the scanning flow instead of converting directly, because it finds the edges and corrects perspective.

Heavy jobs and phone limits

Heavy jobs such as Word and Excel conversion, OCR and compression are not practical on a phone, so they run on the server. They work on mobile too, but the file is uploaded. Structural tasks such as merging and scanning stay entirely on your device.

Work in the browser uses the phone's memory, so processing a few hundred scanned pages can slow down or restart the tab. For files like that, split the document or leave the job to a computer. For everyday documents a phone is more than enough.

item.title: PowerPoint to PDF: What Survives and What Gets Flattened
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: A PDF keeps every slide looking the same for everyone, but it flattens anything interactive. Know what you keep and what you lose before you send the deck.
item.content:encoded:
Sending a deck as a PowerPoint file is a gamble: fonts may shift, animations may break and slides can be changed by accident. A PDF makes the deck look identical for everyone and keeps it from being edited.

PowerPoint to PDF

  1. Upload the deck — Add your .ppt or .pptx file to the PowerPoint to PDF tool.
  2. Convert — All slides are combined into a single PDF with the design preserved.
  3. Download — You get a share-ready deck that looks the same on every device.

PowerPoint to PDF — Convert your deck into a single PDF with the design intact. Open the tool

What survives and what does not

PDF is a fixed output format. It keeps how slides look but flattens everything interactive, and knowing that in advance avoids surprises after you send.

  • Kept: layout, colours, fonts, images, and the appearance of tables and charts.
  • Kept: slide order and aspect ratio (16:9 or 4:3).
  • Lost: transitions and animations, because an animated slide becomes one page in its final state.
  • Lost: embedded video and audio, with only a poster image remaining in place.
  • Not included: speaker notes in the default output.

Why fonts shift, and how PDF stops it

A PowerPoint file often does not embed the typeface and only records its name. If the recipient lacks that font, the program substitutes something similar, lines shift and boxes overflow. A PDF embeds the fonts it uses, so it looks the same wherever it is opened. If you will present from an unfamiliar computer, carrying a PDF copy is the safest route.

Handouts

Printing one slide per page usually wastes paper. After converting, use the page layout tool to place 2 or 4 slides on a sheet. It stays legible and costs less to print, and on a long deck ten pages become three.

Going back to PowerPoint

If you only have the PDF of a deck and want to edit it, you can convert it back, and each page becomes a slide.

PDF to PowerPoint — Turn a PDF deck into editable .pptx slides. PDF to PowerPoint

Be realistic, though. A PDF does not contain the editable structure of slides, so the reverse conversion does not restore the original deck. Text boxes are rebuilt, which is enough to reuse text, copy headings or refresh an old deck. If you need to edit the original design precisely, finding the source file is far less work.

Which direction, when

  • To share, present or archive: PowerPoint to PDF.
  • To edit an old deck or reuse content: PDF to PowerPoint.

A last check before sending

  • Does content that appeared through animation show in the right state?
  • Is the small type in charts and tables readable?
  • Did hidden slides make it into the output, and do you want them there?
  • Does the file size fit the channel you are sharing through?

item.title: Compare Two Contract Versions Without Reading Both
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: 'Only minor edits' is one of the riskiest phrases in a negotiation. A comparison shows what really changed, and which of it deserves a second look.
item.content:encoded:
Is this the same version they sent last week, or did a clause change? Comparing two PDFs by hand is slow and risky, because a single changed date or amount can slip by. AI reduces the job to seconds.

Why manual comparison fails

Reading two long documents side by side demands sustained focus, and across pages of text it is easy to miss an added sentence, a removed exception or a changed figure. Formatting differences such as renumbered clauses and shifted paragraphs can also hide the real changes.

Three steps

  1. Upload both versions — Add document A (old) and document B (new) to the Compare PDF tool.
  2. Compare — The AI understands the text and extracts added, removed and changed clauses.
  3. Review the differences — Look especially at binding changes: amounts, dates, terms, parties, obligations and penalty clauses.

Compare PDF — Compare two versions of a contract and see the binding differences in seconds. Open the tool

Which changes matter

Two versions can differ in dozens of places, but most are cosmetic: a comma, a renumbered clause, a shifted paragraph. The risk concentrates in known places, and those deserve attention first.

  • Amounts: figures, currency and tax wording.
  • Dates and periods: delivery, payment, notice and termination timeframes.
  • Liability: caps, indemnities and penalty clauses.
  • Parties: a changed legal name or an added party.
  • Negative wording such as 'excluding', 'not included' and 'limited to', where a one-word insertion can change the scope entirely.
  • Governing law and jurisdiction.

How quiet changes happen

A common moment in negotiation is the other side sending a new file and saying they made only minor edits. Usually that is true, but the same email can carry a one-word change in a clause nobody discussed. The only reliable way to catch it is to compare the two versions, because memory and goodwill are not enough.

When it helps most

  • Checking contract revisions before you approve them.
  • Seeing what changed in tender or specification updates.
  • Understanding what the other side's minor edits actually contain.

Prepare the inputs

A readable result needs comparable inputs. If one version includes annexes and the other does not, most of the differences come from the annexes and the real changes get lost. Separate the annexes and compare the main texts for a far more readable result. Scanned versions need their text extracted first.

Keep a record

In a negotiation with several rounds it is easy to forget what changed when. Keep each comparison with its date and you can answer when a clause took its current form in minutes. Merging the versions and comparison outputs into one document with page numbers keeps that archive tidy.

What comparison cannot tell you

A comparison shows what changed, not what the change means for you. A raised liability cap is technically a small difference and commercially a large risk. Comparison does not replace legal assessment; it points at what needs assessing, so you can spend your lawyer's time on the right clauses.

To understand not just the difference but the whole document before signing, the Summarize and Chat with PDF tools let you ask questions about it.

Chat with PDF — Ask the document questions such as what the penalty clause says, and get clear answers. Chat tool

item.title: Real PDF Redaction: Remove Personal Data Before Sharing
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Drawing a black rectangle over text leaves the text in the file. Real redaction deletes it. Here is the difference, the fields people forget and a verification routine.
item.content:encoded:
Before you share a contract, invoice or official document, personal data such as ID numbers, IBANs, phone numbers and addresses often has to be hidden, frequently as a legal requirement under GDPR or KVKK. But drawing a black box over text is not real hiding.

Why a black box is not safe

In most tools you hide sensitive data by drawing a black rectangle over it. The original text stays inside the document, so anyone who opens the PDF in a text editor, removes the box or copies the text can read it back. That is a leak and a compliance risk.

Real redaction removes the data from the document's content. Our redaction tool deletes the data entirely instead of covering it, so in the redacted spot searching, copying or recovery is impossible.

Three steps

  1. Upload the PDF — Add your document to the redaction tool.
  2. Sensitive fields are found — Patterns such as ID, IBAN, phone and email are detected on your device, and context-based data such as names and addresses is detected with AI.
  3. Remove permanently — The fields you confirm are truly deleted from the document's content. Download the cleaned PDF.

Redact Sensitive Data — Permanently remove personal data and share the document safely. Open the tool

The part detected on your device (ID, IBAN, phone, email) is not sent anywhere as it is removed. Only context-based detection of names and addresses sends text to the AI.

When you need it

  • Before sharing a contract or invoice with a third party.
  • In official applications, tenders or court files.
  • For documents published as samples or templates.

Fields people overlook

Personal data does not sit only where you expect. When you check the middle of a page before sharing, the details around the edges get skipped, and that is exactly where leaks come from.

  • Names, branch codes or usernames in headers and footers.
  • The signature block and direct phone number of whoever prepared the document.
  • Records belonging to third parties left in annex table rows.
  • Readable details underneath stamp and signature images.
  • A customer number on an invoice, or a full account number on a statement.

Metadata is part of the document

Even with the page cleaned, a document can carry invisible information: the name of whoever created the file, the software used, creation and modification dates, and sometimes a title left from an earlier draft. These sit in the document properties and anyone curious can see them in a couple of clicks. Clearing metadata is the companion step to redaction on documents going outside.

What to hide and what to leave

Over-redacting makes the document useless, and under-redacting leaves the risk in place. The test is the purpose of sending it: which information does the recipient genuinely need to do their job? A lease sent for a loan application needs the rent figure, but usually not the landlord's identity number. Ask that field by field and you end up with a document that is both compliant and usable.

Verify afterwards

  • Reopen the document and search for what you removed. Any result means removal did not happen.
  • Select the text and paste it elsewhere; the redacted part should not appear.
  • Review every page, because the same detail may repeat elsewhere.
  • Check document properties, since a name or file path may remain in the metadata.
  • Save the redacted version under a new name and share from that file.

Scans behave differently

In a scanned document the page is an image. With no text layer there is no text to remove, and covering an area stays permanent on the image. But if the document has been through OCR, an invisible text layer sits beneath it, and the information in that layer can still be copied. With scans, check whether a text layer exists.

item.title: Editing PDF Text: Why a White Box Is Not a Fix
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: A wrong date or price in a PDF is easy to hide and surprisingly hard to really fix. Here is how real editing differs from covering text, and where its limits are.
item.content:encoded:
Fixing a small mistake in a PDF, such as a wrong date, an outdated price or a typo, is harder than it looks. Many online editors do not delete the text at all; they place a white box on top of it. This guide is about real editing.

Covering versus deleting

When a tool just puts a box over the text, the original stays inside the document and can still appear when it is copied or searched. That is messy, and it is a privacy risk. Real editing removes the text from the document and puts new text in its place.

The Edit PDF tool really removes the existing text and writes your new text in its place instead of covering it up. Turkish characters are fully supported.

Four steps

  1. Open the PDF — Upload your document to the Edit PDF tool.
  2. Click the text — Click the text you want to change, and the existing text is selected.
  3. Delete or rewrite — Remove the text or type a replacement. You can add and correct text.
  4. Download — Download the edited PDF, with the change baked into the document.

Edit PDF — Truly delete and replace PDF text, with no covering up. Open the tool

What it needs

The tool works on PDFs that contain a real text layer, for example one exported from Word. In scanned or photo PDFs the text is an image, so you first need to turn it into text with OCR.

OCR a scanned PDF — If your document is scanned, first turn the text into real text with OCR. OCR tool

Why it is not like editing in Word

In Word, text flows, so adding a sentence moves everything after it. In a PDF every piece of text sits at a fixed position on the page and nothing flows. Replacing a word with a longer one does not reflow the line. That is not a shortcoming of the tool but the design of the format, because PDF exists to preserve a printed result.

What to expect while editing

  • If the new text is longer than the old, it can overflow the line, so a short equivalent is the practical fix.
  • If the typeface is not embedded, a similar one is used and a small visual difference can appear.
  • When changing a value in a table cell, check that the alignment still holds.
  • If the same wording appears many times, each occurrence has to be corrected separately.

Edit, or rebuild from the source?

Judge by the size of the change. For a date, amount, name or typo, editing directly is the cleanest route and leaves the rest untouched. If paragraphs will be rewritten, a section added or the layout changed, rebuilding from the source is less work. Without the source, converting to Word, editing and producing a PDF again is a third route, though each round shifts the formatting a little.

A note on official documents

Changing a document's text may be technically possible, but it is not legitimate on every document. Altering an invoice, an official letter, a signed contract or correspondence from an institution destroys the document's standing and can have serious consequences. Editing is for fixing mistakes in documents you produced. Any change to a digitally signed document invalidates the signature, which is a sign the protection works.

Editing is not enough for privacy

If you want information out of a document, deleting the visible text seems to solve it, but traces can remain in metadata, document properties or the same detail on other pages. Where personal data is involved, use a tool that removes content permanently and clear the document's metadata too. A document that looks clean can still be technically unclean.

item.title: Page Numbers for Reports, Theses and Contracts
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Page numbers do more than label pages. In a contract they show nothing is missing, and in a thesis they follow a convention. Here is how to choose well.
item.content:encoded:
In a multi-page document, page numbers keep readers oriented, stop printed pages getting mixed up and make references easy. This guide covers how to add them, and the choices that make them look professional.

When you need them

  • Easy referencing in reports, theses and academic documents.
  • Page integrity in contracts and official paperwork.
  • Keeping order in long documents headed for print.

Three steps

  1. Upload the PDF — Add your document to the Page Numbers tool.
  2. Choose position and format — Set whether the number goes at the top or bottom, and pick its format.
  3. Download — Every page of the numbered PDF is numbered.

Add Page Numbers — Add page numbers to your PDF with your choice of position and format. Open the tool

If your document has a cover page, consider starting numbering from the content page. A cover without a number looks more professional.

Choosing a format

No standard forces your hand, but readers have expectations. An ornate numbering style distracts on official paperwork, while a bare digit can feel thin in a long report.

  • Plain digit (1, 2, 3): the safest choice for most reports, printed slides and everyday documents.
  • Page 1 style: helps orientation when the document will be read on paper.
  • 1 / 12 style: preferred for contracts and quotes, where completeness matters, because the other side can tell whether a page is missing.
  • Roman numerals (i, ii, iii): used for front matter such as preface and contents, with the main text restarting at 1.

Where numbering should start

Cover pages are almost never numbered. A common academic pattern is no number on the cover, roman numerals through the front matter and 1 on the first page of the main text. Corporate reports usually number every page except the cover, starting at 1.

If the organization receiving the document has a style guide, the choice may not be yours. University thesis guides and public-sector standards often state the position and format explicitly, and checking first is cheaper than preparing the document twice.

Finish the page order first

Page numbers are printed into the document. Adding, deleting or reordering pages afterwards leaves numbers that no longer match the content, and a second page reading 3 tells the reader the document was put together carelessly.

  • Add missing pages, delete unnecessary ones and settle the order first.
  • If you are merging several files, merge before you number.
  • Fix sideways pages first, since the number is placed relative to page orientation.
  • Leave numbering as the last step.

When the number hits existing content

Some documents have narrow bottom margins, and the number collides with a footnote or a table row. There are two practical fixes: move the number to the top edge, or adjust the margin with the crop tool before numbering. Neither touches the text of the document.

Common mistakes

  • Adding pages after numbering, so the numbers drift out of sync with the content.
  • Numbering the cover as well, which looks amateurish on official documents.
  • Adding a second layer of numbers to a document that already has them, so check first.
  • Aligning numbers for single-sided pages on a document that will be printed double-sided.

item.title: CamScanner Alternative: Free, Watermark-Free, Private

item.title: Scan a Document With Your Phone Camera and No App
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Most scanner apps want an account, show ads or upload your files. A browser-based scanner does the same job on your device, so the page never leaves your phone.
item.content:encoded:
You have a paper document and you need it as a PDF quickly. The usual route is to install a scanner app and accept the ads, the sign-up screens and the permissions that send your files to the cloud. There is another way: do the whole job in your phone's browser, with nothing to install and nothing uploaded.

What changes when it runs in the browser

The PDF Platform scanner opens in your phone browser, and edge detection, perspective correction and PDF creation all happen on your device. You get no install, and your document is never uploaded.

Four taps

  2. Point at the document — The edges are marked live with a green outline. Hold steady and the system captures the page by itself, with no shutter press needed.

Several pages, one PDF

item.title: Document Photo to Clean PDF: Straighten and Filter
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: A photographed page is slanted, has a desk behind it and a shadow on one side. Four corners and a lighting correction turn it into something that looks scanned.
item.content:encoded:
Photographing a page is easy. Getting a result that looks like a scan is harder: the document is slanted, the desk is in frame and one corner is in shadow. That is exactly where a good scanner steps in and turns the photo into a flat, clean document.

Perspective correction

Because you rarely shoot perfectly top-down, the edges are not parallel and the page looks slanted. The scanner finds the four corners automatically and recomputes the image so the document becomes a flat rectangle, as if viewed head-on. The desk behind it is cropped away.

Shadow removal and contrast

Handheld shots rarely have even light, with one edge dark and another bright. The Auto filter estimates the background lighting on each colour channel and balances it, removing shadows and flattening the background toward white. Text sharpens and colours stay, much like the magic colour effect in scanner apps.

Which filter for which page

  • Color: invoices with logos and documents with photographs.
  • Gray: text-heavy documents, with a smaller file.
  • Black and White: the sharpest text and smallest file, ideal for plain text.
  • Auto (Pro): shadow removal plus contrast, for the most professional, scanner-like output.

Getting a good capture

  1. Good light, flat surface — Place the page on a flat surface and shoot from above without casting a shadow. Keep contrast between the surface and the page so the edges are easy to find.
  2. Wait for auto-capture — Hold the camera steady. The edges are marked with a green outline and the page is captured by itself.
  3. Pick a filter and create — Choose the right filter for the document and create the PDF, adjusting corners if needed.

Image to PDF — Turn your document photos into a single PDF, on your device and with no sign-up. Open the tool

If the file is large after scanning, use Compress to reduce its size. To reorder, rotate or delete pages, open the scanned PDF directly in the matching tool.

item.title: Searchable PDF: Why Ctrl+F Fails on Scans and How OCR Helps
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: If Ctrl+F finds nothing in your scan, the words are pixels, not text. A searchable PDF puts real text behind the picture and the document looks exactly the same.
item.content:encoded:
When you scan a document to PDF, the writing inside is not text to a computer. It is an image made of pixels, which is why you cannot search for a word or copy a sentence. A searchable PDF solves exactly that.

What is inside a searchable PDF

It has an invisible text layer embedded over the scanned image and aligned to each word. You still see the photograph, but real, selectable text sits behind it. You can search with Ctrl+F and copy text, and archive and document systems can search by content.

How OCR builds that layer

OCR, or optical character recognition, reads the text in the image and works out each word and its position. Those words are then placed invisibly over the image at their exact locations. The document looks untouched, yet it is searchable inside.

Make one in three steps

  1. Scan or upload — Use the phone document scanner, or open a scanned PDF you already have.
  2. Choose Make searchable — After creating the PDF in the scanner, use Make searchable. Text is recognized on your device (Turkish and English).
  3. Save and search — Save the resulting PDF. Ctrl+F and copy now work in any PDF viewer.

OCR runs entirely on your device, including Turkish characters such as ş, ğ, ı and İ. Your document is never sent to a server for recognition. Searchable PDF output is a Pro feature.

Scanned PDF to Text (OCR) — Just want the text? Convert a scanned PDF to plain text on your device. Open the OCR tool

Where it earns its keep

  • Archiving: search by keyword across hundreds of scanned documents.
  • Legal and accounting work: find an amount or clause in a contract or invoice instantly.
  • Students: search topics in photos of lecture notes.
  • Accessibility: screen readers can read the document.

item.title: PDF Watermark Guide: Wording, Opacity and Limits
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: A watermark is a quick way to label status and ownership. It is a deterrent, not a lock, so the wording and the settings matter more than the stamp itself.
item.content:encoded:
A watermark lays a semi-transparent line of text over every page to show the document's status (draft, confidential, copy) or its owner. It is useful when you share contracts, send quotes or want people to think twice before passing a file on.

What it is good for

  • Stating status: DRAFT, CONFIDENTIAL, NOT APPROVED.
  • Stamping ownership or brand: your company name or website.
  • Discouraging sharing: the semi-transparent text stays visible even in screenshots.

Four steps

  1. Upload the PDF — Choose the document you want to watermark.
  2. Type the text — Enter wording such as DRAFT, CONFIDENTIAL or your company name.
  3. Set colour, font and opacity — Pick the colour (#RRGGBB), the font and an opacity that keeps the document readable.
  4. Preview and download — Check the preview and, if it looks right, download the watermarked PDF.

Too strong and the text is hard to read; too faint and it is barely visible. An opacity of 10 to 20 percent works for most documents.

Add Watermark — Stamp DRAFT, CONFIDENTIAL or your brand in minutes. Open the tool

Choosing the wording

A watermark works only as well as it is clear. A page stamped Copy says little. One stamped Copy, 12 Mar 2026, Accounting tells you where it came from if it leaks. Three approaches are common in business:

  • Status: DRAFT, NOT APPROVED or CANCELLED signals that the document is not in force.
  • Confidentiality: CONFIDENTIAL, INTERNAL or DO NOT DISTRIBUTE reminds the reader of their duty.
  • Traceability: the recipient's name or a date shows which copy a leak came from.

Keep it readable

The most common mistake is making the document unreadable. A diagonal placement crosses fewer lines than a horizontal one and tires the eye less. Check at 100 percent zoom and, if you can, in print, because a watermark that looks faint on screen can print darker than you expect.

A deterrent, not protection

A watermark does not stop anyone copying, printing or forwarding the document. It only makes clear that whoever shared it did so knowingly. For real protection, encrypt with a password. The two do not replace each other and are often combined on sensitive files: the watermark reminds people of their duty, and the password limits who can open it.

  • To password-protect: Encrypt PDF.
  • For page numbers: Add Page Numbers.
  • If you need a signature: Sign PDF.

Keeping versions apart

When five versions of one contract circulate, working out which is current gets hard, and signing the wrong one is a real risk. Marking drafts with a watermark that carries the version and date largely prevents that. When the final version is ready, produce a clean copy from the source rather than trying to strip the watermark out.

Before you stamp

  • Is the content final? The layout will not shift, but changed content means starting again.
  • On multi-page documents the watermark applies to every page, so keep the cover separate if you do not want it there.
  • Pick a colour that does not clash with the document's own colours.
  • Save the watermarked version under a new name and keep the original clean.

item.title: Sign a PDF Online: Draw, Type or Upload Your Signature
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Printing, signing and scanning a contract wastes time and quality. Signing the PDF directly takes a minute, and nothing leaves your device.
item.content:encoded:
Print, sign by hand, scan back: slow, and the result looks worse each time. Signing the PDF itself is faster and cleaner, and here it happens without an account and without your file leaving your device.

Visual signature or qualified signature?

In everyday use, signing a PDF means placing your signature image on the document. That is enough for most contracts, quotes, rental forms and letters. A qualified electronic signature (QES), which some authorities require, needs a separate certificate or device. This tool provides the first kind: quick, visible signature placement.

Three ways to create your signature

  • Draw: the most natural option with a finger on a touch screen.
  • Type: your name is turned into a handwriting font.
  • Upload: add your stamp or signature image; a transparent PNG works best.

Sign in four steps

  1. Open the PDF — Drag and drop or choose the contract or form. The file opens in your browser.
  2. Create your signature — Click Add signature to draw, type or upload it. It is placed in the centre of the page as soon as it is created.
  3. Place and adjust — Drag it into position, resize from the corner, rotate with the top handle and adjust opacity if needed. You can add a date or text too.
  4. Apply and download — For multi-page files use Apply to all pages to copy it to the same spot, then click Apply and download. Your signed PDF is ready.

Your signature and file are not uploaded. Signing happens entirely in your browser, on your device, so you can sign confidential documents safely.

Sign PDF — Sign your contract in seconds, with no sign-up and on your device. Open the tool

A signature on every page

Multi-page contracts often need a signature or initials on each page. Place yours once and click Apply to all pages to copy it to the same position everywhere. You can also use Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V to copy an item elsewhere.

Add a date and a note

Next to the signature you can add a date and free text, for example 'Read and approved', choose any text colour and position everything by dragging. It is all written into the PDF in one pass.

item.title: Mark Up a PDF: Highlight, Draw and Add Notes
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Reviewing a document, you want a pen in your hand. Markup adds highlights, drawings and notes on top of the page and leaves the original text exactly as it was.
item.content:encoded:
Reviewing a contract, an assignment or a report, you want to highlight the key sentence, jot a note, box a clause or point with an arrow. Markup PDF lets you do exactly that in the browser, and your file never leaves your device.

The tools

  • Highlighter: paints over text semi-transparently, so the text below stays readable.
  • Pen: freehand drawing, with a straight-line mode as well.
  • Box and Arrow: frame a region or point to it.
  • Text: write a note in the margin or on the document.

Four steps

  1. Open the PDF — Drag and drop or choose the document you want to mark up.
  2. Pick a tool and colour — Highlighter, pen, box, arrow or text, then a colour and thickness.
  3. Draw on the page — Drag to mark. Marker and pen offer a Straight mode for drawing cleanly over lines of text.
  4. Edit and download — Use Select to move, resize or recolour a mark, and undo with Ctrl+Z. Then click Apply and download.

Marks are added on top of the document. Existing text is never removed or changed, and highlighter and pen are semi-transparent so the text below stays readable.

Markup PDF — Mark up your document with highlights, drawings and notes, on your device and with no sign-up. Open the tool

Markup, editing and redaction are different

The three look alike, yet the results differ completely, and picking the wrong one causes problems.

  • Markup adds a layer over the document. The text underneath stays readable and searchable, which makes it right for review and feedback.
  • Editing actually changes the text in the document. This is what you need to correct a wrong date or amount.
  • Redaction removes the text from the document. It is the only correct method for hiding personal data, because drawing a black box is not enough.

Notes that others can act on

Markup someone else will read is different from a note to yourself. A highlighted paragraph leaves the reader asking what about it, while a one-sentence note noticeably reduces the number of rounds. Let colour carry meaning, for example yellow for attention, red for must change and green for approved, and explain the scheme in a note at the start.

A three-pass order for contract review

Following a set order rather than marking as you go speeds up a legal or commercial review and prevents omissions. First mark everything containing an amount, date or duration. Then mark the sentences that create obligations. Last, mark the wording you find unclear. That sweep is more reliable than reading end to end once.

Sharing the marked-up file

Because marks are written into the document, the recipient sees your notes in any viewer without special software. That does not mean they cannot be removed, and a clean version has to be regenerated from the original. Save the marked-up version under a new name and keep the original clean.

Download the marked-up PDF and send it by email. If you also need a signature use Sign PDF, and for text corrections use Edit PDF on the same document.

How it prints

A highlight that reads comfortably on screen can become a grey band over the text in black-and-white print. If the document will be printed, prefer light colours and put the important information in the note rather than the colour. In greyscale colours converge, so marks distinguished only by colour lose their meaning on paper.

item.title: How to Rearrange PDF Pages and Fix Backwards Scans
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Two-sided scans often arrive as 1, 3, 5 and then 6, 4, 2. The content is all there; only the order needs fixing. Here is how to do it quickly.
item.content:encoded:
A batch scanner that delivers pages in reverse, an annex that belongs at the front, a flow that makes more sense in a different sequence: rearranging PDF pages is much easier than most people expect.

When you need it

  • Fixing pages a batch scanner delivered in reverse order.
  • Moving an annex or cover to the front or back.
  • Tidying the flow after merging several documents.
  • Putting sections in a logical order before a presentation.

Three steps

  1. Open the PDF — Drop your file into the Organize pages tool. Pages appear as numbered thumbnails.
  2. Set the new order — Move pages with the up and down buttons, or type a target position number. The new order shows instantly.
  3. Download — Confirm and download the rearranged PDF. Your original stays unchanged.

Organize pages — Rearrange pages in seconds, with no signup and on your device. Open the tool

  • To remove pages, use the Delete Pages tool.
  • To fix sideways pages, use Rotate PDF.
  • To combine two documents into one, use Merge PDF.

As a guest, reordering runs entirely in your browser and your file is not uploaded.

The batch-scanner order fault

Automatic feeders often mishandle double-sided documents. The device scans all the fronts first, then all the backs after you flip the stack, leaving pages arranged 1, 3, 5 and then 6, 4, 2. The document looks unreadable but the content is complete, and all it needs is a corrected order. Knowing this saves you from rescanning.

Plan the order before you move anything

Moving pages one at a time through a long document is tiring. Decide the target order first, meaning which section opens, where the annexes go and where the signature page sits, and then move pages in large blocks rather than individually. The numbers on the thumbnails tell you where you are as you go.

Two things people forget

  • Page numbers: if numbers are printed into the document, they no longer match. Number after reordering, not before.
  • Contents pages and cross-references: phrases like 'see page 12' shift, so long documents need a review.

If the document will be printed and bound

For double-sided printing, starting each section on an odd page is the usual convention, with a blank inserted where needed. For a booklet, the page order is not the reading order at all, because sheets are arranged so that folding produces the right sequence. Leave that imposition to a page layout tool; it is faster and less error-prone than working it out by hand.

Reorder or merge?

Rearranging pages inside one document and bringing several documents together are different jobs. If you have separate files, merge them into one document first and then rearrange. Inside a single file, reordering alone is enough.

Review before downloading

An order can look right when you only check the sequence of numbers, but the real test is the flow of content. Glance at the first page, the section transitions and the last page before downloading, so an out-of-order document never goes out.

item.title: Why Your PDF Opens Sideways, and How to Fix It
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: The rotate button in a PDF viewer only turns your screen. Here is how to change the pages themselves, so they look right for everyone who opens the file.
item.content:encoded:
Scans and phone photos often produce sideways or upside-down pages. Pressing rotate in a viewer fixes what you see, but reopen the file and the page is sideways again. The lasting fix is to rotate the pages and save them that way.

View rotation versus saved rotation

Every PDF page carries its own orientation. A viewer's rotate button usually changes only the on-screen view and does not write that choice into the file. Close it, send it to someone or print it, and the page is sideways again. Saved rotation changes the orientation itself, so the document looks right in any program and in print.

Three steps

  1. Open the PDF — Drop your file into the Rotate PDF tool. Each page appears as a thumbnail.
  2. Set the orientation — Use the left and right buttons on each card to turn pages in 90 degree steps. Fix only the sideways pages, or all of them.
  3. Download — Confirm and download. The new PDF has the correct orientation every time it opens.

Rotate PDF — Turn sideways scans the right way up and save permanently, on your device with no signup. Open the tool

  • If only one page is sideways, rotate just that page.
  • Fix upside-down (180 degree) pages by rotating twice.
  • Afterwards, clear out unwanted pages with the Delete Pages tool.

As a guest, rotation runs entirely in your browser. Your file is not uploaded, and it keeps working if your connection drops.

Why pages end up sideways

A sideways page is usually a faithful record of how it was captured rather than a fault. There are three common causes: the sheet was placed on the scanner in landscape, the automatic feeder pulled some sheets the wrong way round, or the phone recorded its orientation while shooting and the PDF builder ignored it. All three have the same fix: rotate the page and save it that way.

Documents with mixed orientations

A report may deliberately mix portrait text pages with landscape tables, and turning everything the same way would make the tables unreadable. In those documents, fix only the pages that are genuinely wrong. Skim the thumbnails and select just the upside-down or wrongly oriented pages; it takes seconds.

Why it matters in print and for submissions

A sideways page is annoying on screen but a real problem on paper. The printer may shrink the page, cut the edges or print it landscape. On documents going to an institution, wrong orientation can be grounds for rejection on legibility. Checking every page before sending is cheaper than sending twice.

What to do next

  • Clear out blank or duplicate pages.
  • Fix the page order if scanning disturbed it, which is common.
  • If you will make a scan searchable, run OCR after rotating, because recognition drops on skewed pages.
  • Add page numbers last, so they sit according to each page's new orientation.

Avoiding the problem at the scanner

The easiest fix is not needing one. Choose the correct paper orientation on the scanner, load the feeder with the stack facing the same way, and hold the phone parallel to the page. That removes most of the work that would otherwise follow.

item.title: Remove Pages From a PDF Without Uploading It
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Deleting pages takes seconds. Knowing which pages to remove, and what deleting cannot hide, is what keeps documents clean and safe to share.
item.content:encoded:
A blank page from a scanner, a document that arrived twice, a section that should not leave the building: removing PDF pages is one of the most common edits there is. It needs no installation and no account.

Typical reasons

  • Cleaning out blank or duplicate pages a scanner added.
  • Taking internal or confidential pages out of a report before sharing.
  • Dropping repeated cover pages in a merged document.
  • Keeping only the section you need.

Why on-device deletion is better

Many online tools upload your file to their servers. Used as a guest, page deletion here runs entirely in your browser, so the file never travels over the internet. That is better for privacy and for speed, since there is no upload wait and it even works offline.

Three steps

  1. Open the PDF — Drop it into the Delete Pages tool. Every page appears as a thumbnail.
  2. Select pages to remove — Click the pages you want to drop. The new order of the remaining pages appears immediately.
  3. Download — Confirm and download the cleaned PDF. Your original stays untouched, and a new copy is created.

Delete Pages — Remove blank or unwanted pages in seconds, with no signup and on your device. Open the tool

If you want to keep only a few pages out of many, splitting those pages out with Split PDF may be faster than deleting the rest.

  • To reorder pages as well, use the Organize pages tool.
  • Picked the wrong page? Deselect it before downloading.
  • Because it runs on your device, reasonably sized files finish instantly.

Deleting a page is not the same as hiding text

A deleted page genuinely does not appear in the new file, and its content is not carried over. People often confuse this with hiding a few lines on a page. Drawing a black box over them is not enough, because the box sits on top while the text underneath remains in the file and can still be copied. Delete when a whole page must go, and use a tool that removes content permanently when only part of a page must go.

What to pull out before sharing

Pages nobody remembered to remove are the most ordinary kind of leak. In corporate documents these are the ones that reach the other side unnecessarily:

  • Annexes holding internal pricing, cost or margin.
  • Template pages still carrying details of a previous client.
  • Signature routing sheets and internal approval forms.
  • Old version pages stamped as drafts.
  • Copies of identity or personnel documents holding personal data.

What scanners leave behind

Scanners with automatic feeders save blank reverse sides as pages when scanning double-sided. A twenty-page document becomes forty and the file size doubles. A page may also have been scanned twice after a paper jam. Skim the thumbnails and remove blanks and duplicates, and the file shrinks and becomes readable.

After deleting

  • Existing page numbers no longer match the content, so number after deleting, not before.
  • Page references in a contents section shift; check them on long documents.
  • If the document shrank a lot, compression may no longer be needed; measure once.
  • Save the trimmed version under a new name and keep the complete original in your archive.

Delete or split?

If you will send five pages out of a hundred, selecting ninety-five makes no sense, and extracting the pages you need is quicker. As a rough rule, keeping the majority means delete, and keeping the minority means split.

item.title: Split a PDF: Extract Pages, Sections or Every Page
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Often you need only the signature page or one section. Splitting gets you exactly that, and sending less is also a good privacy habit.
item.content:encoded:
Sometimes the whole document is not what you need: the signature page of a contract, one section of a report, or a smaller part that fits an email. Splitting a PDF is built for that.

What people use it for

  • Extracting only the pages you need from a thick document.
  • Breaking one PDF into sections to share separately.
  • Cutting a large file into smaller parts for an email attachment.
  • Saving each page as its own PDF.

Three steps

  1. Open the PDF — Drop your file into the Split PDF tool. Pages are listed in a preview grid.
  2. Select pages or a range — Mark the pages you want. They can be combined into one PDF or saved as separate files.
  3. Download — Download the result as a single PDF, or as separate files inside a ZIP.

Split PDF — Pull out the pages you need in seconds, with no signup and on your device. Open the tool

Split or delete?

If you want to keep just a few pages, splitting them out is the most practical. If you want to keep most pages and drop a few, Delete Pages is faster. Both run on your device.

  • To recombine parts into one file, use the Merge PDF tool.
  • If pages are out of order, fix them first with Organize pages.
  • Because it runs in your browser, your file is not sent over the internet.

Finding the pages you want

Locating where a section starts and ends can take longer than the split itself. If there is a contents page, read the range from there. If not and the document is searchable, search for a keyword. For scans, make the document searchable with OCR first, which is far more efficient than paging through it.

Share only what is needed

Sending the whole document is usually habit, not necessity. If someone asked for the signature page of a lease, one month of a statement or the financial section of a report, sending everything shares information nobody needed. It is also the right habit for personal data: give the other side enough to do their job, and no more.

Fitting a big file into an email

When a document exceeds the attachment limit you can compress or split. Compression works well on scans but is not always enough. Splitting into sensible parts and sending them in order is then the cleanest answer. Cut at section boundaries rather than arbitrarily, and name the files so the recipient can open them in sequence.

Naming the parts

  • Put the document name and page range in the file name, such as contract-p12-18.pdf.
  • Put the sequence at the end rather than the start so alphabetical sorting still works.
  • If you add a date, use year-month-day, which sorts correctly on its own.
  • State the number of parts, such as 1 of 3 and 2 of 3, so a missing part is noticed immediately.

Putting the parts back together

Splitting is reversible, because the parts can be merged back into one file. That helps if you want to work through a document section by section and combine it at the end. Check the order while merging; file names sort alphabetically, so naming them properly at the start pays off.

When splitting is not enough

If the information that must stay private sits inside a page, extracting that page does not help, because the information travels with the part. You then need to remove the page or permanently remove the area in question. A box drawn on top is not enough, since the text underneath stays in the file.

item.title: Bank Statement PDF to Excel: Get Clean Transaction Columns
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Copying a statement out of a PDF scrambles the columns. Here is how to extract the transactions cleanly, verify them and import them without regional-format surprises.
item.content:encoded:
Month-end bookkeeping, expense tracking and budgeting all start with the same chore: getting transactions from a PDF statement into a spreadsheet. Banks do not issue PDFs as clean tables, so copy and paste breaks the alignment.

Why the PDF resists

Rows look tidy on the page, but there is no table structure behind them. Copied dates, descriptions and amounts land in one cell or the wrong columns. AI recognizes the structure and divides it into the right columns.

Three steps

  1. Upload the statement PDF — Add it to the Extract Data tool. Text is read on your device.
  2. Click Extract Data — The AI turns transactions into a structured table of date, description and amount.
  3. Download the CSV — Open it in Excel, where you can filter and total.

Export Statement to Excel — Turn bank statement transactions into a tidy table. Open the tool

With statements for several months, use AI Batch to process them all and merge them into one CSV.

Check whether your bank already offers CSV

Online banking often offers formats other than PDF, and most people never notice. If you only need the numbers and your bank can export CSV or Excel directly, that is the cleanest route. Often, though, a PDF is all you have: it came by email, from an archive, or the bank only offers PDF for older periods. This method is for that case.

Verify the extracted table

Do not feed unchecked data straight into your books. A few minutes of review costs far less than hunting for a balance that will not reconcile at month-end.

  • Row count: does the number of transactions match the statement?
  • Totals: do credits and debits agree with the statement's summary section?
  • Date format: has the day and month order been swapped, especially on ambiguous dates like 01/02?
  • Decimal separator: comma or point, and whether amounts break when opened in Excel.
  • Sign: did debits come through as negatives, or in a separate column?

Opening a CSV without damaging it

Double-clicking a CSV can mangle amounts depending on your regional settings. A number with a decimal comma may turn into text or be mistaken for a date. Open Excel empty and import through Data, From Text/CSV, choosing the delimiter and column formats yourself. Once set up, repeat the same steps every month.

Many months, many accounts

A yearly breakdown means twelve statements. Processing them one by one and pasting results underneath each other is slow and error-prone, so run them together as a batch and collect one table. If you combine several accounts, add an account column to make filtering easy.

Protect what you share

A statement carries your account number and a picture of how you spend. Before sending it to an accountant or a third party, remove what they do not need, such as part of the account number, your address or unrelated periods, using the redaction tool. Covering text with a box is not enough, because the text underneath can still be copied.

item.content:encoded:
Contract annexes, scanned pages, a stack of reports: you want one file, not six. The merge tool does it inside your browser, so there is nothing to install and no account to make.

Why on-device merging is different

Most online tools send your files to their servers. Here the merge happens on your device and nothing goes over the internet. That helps privacy and speed alike: no upload wait, and the result is immediate.

Three steps

  1. Add your PDFs — Drag them in or select several at once. Up to 80 MB in total, with no limit on the number of files.
  2. Put them in order — Use the up and down arrows. The document is built in the order you see.
  3. Merge and save — Press Merge. One PDF is produced immediately and saved where you choose.

Merge PDF — Add your files, set the order and download one PDF for free. Open the tool

Quick tips

  • Turning JPG or PNG images into a PDF? Use the Image to PDF tool.
  • Need only some pages? Split them out first with the Split tool.
  • It works even offline, because everything happens on your device.

A password-protected PDF has to be unlocked first with the Unlock PDF tool before it can be merged.

Ordering mistakes cost more than technical ones

Computers sort file names by characters, not by numbers, so annex-10 lands before annex-2. Look over the order once after adding the files; that is quicker than rebuilding a merged document.

  • Name annexes 01, 02, 10 so sorting behaves.
  • Cover or letter first, then annexes in the order the contract mentions them.
  • If the front and back of a document are separate files, check the sides line up.
  • A glance at each file's first page avoids adding the wrong one.

What to do after merging

A freshly merged file is rarely ready to send as it is. Page numbers, compression and a tidy first page change how it is received.

  • Add page numbers so the reader can see all annexes arrived.
  • Compress it if it is large, since merged scans quickly pass email limits.
  • Delete stray blank pages, especially scanned reverse sides.
  • Remove sensitive information permanently before sending.

Why it needs no server

Merging does not reprocess content. The page objects are simply rearranged into one file, which a browser can do alone. With no server involved there is nothing to meter, so there is no daily allowance, hourly cap or account. Word conversion and OCR genuinely need computation, so they run on a server. That is the difference.

Mixed page sizes and orientations

Putting a landscape table into an A4 contract leaves a file with mixed sizes. It is not an error and looks fine on screen, but a printer may scale pages differently. If you will print it, bring the pages to the same orientation before merging.

item.title: Reading a Tender Document: A Bid Manager's Order
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Winning or being disqualified often hinges on a handful of clauses buried in dozens of pages. Read them in the right order and you decide faster and miss less.
item.content:encoded:
Tender documents are long, technical and dense, yet the outcome often hinges on a few critical clauses. Experienced bid writers do not read from page one; they first decide whether the bid is worth making.

Reading order

  1. Qualification criteria. If you do not meet the experience, turnover or capacity requirements, reading the rest is pointless.
  2. Submission deadline. Is the remaining preparation time realistic?
  3. Scope. Can you deliver the work yourself, or will you need a subcontractor?
  4. Bonds and payment terms. Does your cash flow support them?
  5. Technical detail last, and only once you have decided to bid.

Clauses to find every time

  • Parties: the awarding body and what it expects of the bidder.
  • Scope: exactly what is required and the delivery terms.
  • Required documents and qualification criteria, such as experience and capacity.
  • Deposit amount and type (bid or performance bond).
  • Submission deadline and time; miss it and you are out.
  • Withdrawal penalty, late penalties and termination clauses.
  • Evaluation criteria: lowest price, or most economically advantageous offer?

Let AI do the first pass

The AI Summarize tool recognizes a tender and brings those clauses forward as a structured summary: parties, deposit, deadline, penalty and evaluation criteria. You see what you would be bidding on without reading 40 pages.

  1. Upload the tender PDF — Text is read on your device, with OCR if it is scanned.
  2. Click Generate Summary — Get a summary highlighting parties, critical dates and amounts, and obligations.
  3. Ask about unclear points — For a question such as the deposit rate, use AI Chat to ask the document directly.

AI Tender Summary — See the critical clauses of a tender in seconds. Open the tool

The AI summary is for quick comprehension. Verify critical clauses in the original text before bidding or making a legal assessment.

How bids get disqualified on formalities

The most frustrating way to lose is not on price but on a formality. These failures have nothing to do with the substance of the bid and are entirely preventable.

  • A required document is missing or out of date.
  • A bid bond's amount or validity does not match the tender.
  • The bid is not submitted in the required form, such as a sealed envelope or a digitally signed file.
  • The total on the unit price schedule does not match the figure in the bid letter.
  • The cut-off time is missed; last-minute uploads to online systems are risky.

Follow the addenda

After publication the awarding body may issue clarifications or amendments. They usually change dates, technical specifications or the list of required documents, and they take precedence over the original text. A bid prepared against the old version can be invalid even if it is otherwise correct. A comparison tool that extracts the difference between two versions is faster and more reliable than reading by hand.

Share only what each person needs

The technical section concerns engineering, the financial section concerns accounting, and the administrative section concerns the bid manager. Splitting out the relevant page ranges raises the chance each section is read and speeds up replies. Attach the summary too, so the team understands the context without opening the whole file.

Keep a clean record

Tender processes can be audited later. Keep the version you downloaded, every addendum and all correspondence, with dates, in one folder, and you can answer which version you bid against in minutes. Merging the documents into one PDF and adding page numbers keeps that archive tidy.

item.title: Invoice PDF to Excel: Totals and Lines Without Retyping
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform

item.content:encoded:
If your month-end includes copying numbers from PDF invoices into a spreadsheet, you know how much time it eats. This guide ranks the three ways of doing it, from slowest to fastest, and walks through the quickest one.

Why a PDF will not simply give you a table

A PDF is built to look the same everywhere, not to hand over data. Invoice numbers, dates, totals and line items look neat on the page but are not stored as a table. Every supplier also lays things out differently, so copy and paste usually lands values in the wrong cells.

Approach 1: type it in

Fine for a couple of invoices a month. Beyond that it is slow, repetitive and the errors are inevitable.

  • Good: needs no extra tools.
  • Bad: slow and prone to mistakes.
  • Best for: a few invoices a month.

Approach 2: OCR, then tidy by hand

For scanned PDFs, our OCR converts the image to real text on your device (Turkish and English), and the file is never uploaded.

Approach 3: let AI read the document

  2. Click Extract Data — The AI identifies the document type and returns fields such as invoice number, date, seller and buyer, tax ID, subtotal, VAT and total, plus any line items, as structured data.
  3. Review and export — See the fields and tables, then export to CSV for Excel or to JSON in one click.

Extract Data — Try one invoice and watch fields and line items become a table in seconds. Open the tool

From one invoice to a whole folder

  • Live progress for each file.
  • All invoices' fields combine under one CSV header.
