item.title: AI Summaries: Key Points From a 50-Page Contract
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: You rarely need every page; you need to know what it says and what to watch for. Here is how to get that quickly and how far to trust it.
item.content:encoded:
When a long contract, tender or report arrives, the real question is simple: what does it say, and what should I watch for? A good AI summary answers that in seconds instead of an hour of reading.

More than a shorter copy

A useful summary does not just cut words. It recognizes the type of document and brings forward what matters. The AI Summarize tool distinguishes tenders, contracts, academic papers and financial reports, and highlights parties, key dates, amounts and obligations.

How to run it

  1. Upload the PDF — Text is read on your device, with OCR for scans. Your file is not uploaded; only the text goes to the AI.
  2. Click Generate Summary — You get a structured summary with title, parties, key points, critical dates and amounts, and takeaways.
  3. Download or share — Save the summary as a clean PDF or pass it on.

AI Summarize — Turn a long document into a professional summary in seconds. Open the tool

If one specific question remains after the summary, ask the document directly with the AI Chat tool.

Prepare the input

A summary is only as good as the text the model sees. Giving it the relevant section of a two-hundred-page file produces a shorter and more accurate result than giving it everything. Separate annexes from the main text, remove unrelated periods and repeated boilerplate, and turn scans into clean pages first.

Verify before you rely on it

A summary shows you where to read; it does not replace reading. For any decision, check the critical facts against the document. The list is short and predictable:

  • Amounts and currency.
  • Dates, durations and notice periods.
  • Party names and signing authority.
  • Penalty, security and termination conditions.
  • Negative provisions such as 'excluded', 'not included' and 'limited to', which fade easily in a summary.

Each document type answers a different question

In a tender, the submission deadline and the security amount should stand out. In a financial report, look for period comparisons and movement in line items. A contract turns on parties and obligations, and a technical report on method and findings. Asking what actually matters in this kind of document makes gaps obvious.

When a summary is only a starting point

Contracts you will sign, notices with legal effect, medical reports and correspondence with public bodies belong here. The summary tells you which clause to discuss and with whom, and the right move is to take it to the relevant expert rather than decide on the summary alone.

Then ask questions

A summary gives the overall picture, but usually one concrete question remains, such as the cancellation fee or whether a clause binds you. Asking the document directly is quicker, because the answer rests on its own text and points to the relevant section.

item.title: Translate a PDF Into Another Language, Keep the Layout
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Pasting a PDF into a translation page destroys its structure. Here is a way to translate that keeps headings, lists and tables, and an honest list of its limits.
item.content:encoded:
Reading a contract, paper or manual in a language you do not know is a common problem, and most solutions wreck the formatting on the way. This guide covers a method that keeps the document's structure intact, plus the cases where machine translation is not enough.

What goes wrong with copy and paste

Copy text into a translation page and headings, lists and tables vanish. On long documents the result becomes unmanageable, and numbers, dates and proper nouns have to survive untouched.

Translating with structure kept

The AI Translate tool translates meaning and layout together:

  1. Upload the PDF — Text is read on your device, with OCR for scans. Your file is not uploaded; only the text goes to translation.
  2. Choose the target language — Pick from 12+ languages, including English, German, French, Spanish, Arabic and Russian.
  3. Translate and download — Headings, lists and tables are preserved. Copy the result or download it as a clean PDF.

AI Translate — Translate your PDF into any language with structure preserved, and download it as a PDF. Open the tool

Where a human translator is still required

AI translation is excellent for speed and understanding. Anything that needs legal weight, such as a notary, a court or an official application, requires a sworn translator. Use AI for a fast first reading and a draft.

To grasp what a long document is about before translating, generate a summary first with the AI Summarize tool.

Prepare the file first

Translation works on the text taken from the document, so clean extraction means accurate translation. In a scan, skewed pages and shadows reduce recognition, and every word lost there is missing from the translation. Straightening pages and making the document searchable first is the cheapest quality gain you can make.

Leave these untranslated

  • Names of people, organizations and brands.
  • Addresses, especially if they will be used for international post.
  • Product codes, serial numbers and reference numbers.
  • Names of legislation and clause numbers.
  • Currency abbreviations and technical units.

Checking these first when you review a translation catches the easiest errors.

Be careful with technical and legal text

Field-specific terms can differ from everyday meanings. In law, indemnity, warranty and liability map differently between legal systems, and in technical writing the same word is read differently across industries. Use the translation to understand, and for a binding decision go back to the original and, if needed, a specialist.

Keep original and translation together

When working across languages, merge the original and the translation into one document. You can then point to the text the other side sees while you discuss a clause, which is the most practical way for a team to be sure everyone means the same thing.

What to do next

  • Summarize a long document for its key points.
  • Ask the document directly about a clause you do not follow.
  • Extract the differences if you have two versions.
  • Remove unnecessary personal data before sharing the translation.

item.title: Screening Research Papers Faster for Literature Reviews
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: The skill in a literature review is not reading everything. It is deciding quickly what deserves a full read. A staged method plus structured summaries gets you there.
item.content:encoded:
For a thesis, assignment or research project, reading dozens of papers in full is nearly impossible. The real skill is screening quickly for the papers that will actually enter your review.

Four things to find fast

  • Research question or hypothesis: what does it ask?
  • Method: what kind of study is it, such as an experiment, survey or meta-analysis?
  • Findings: what did it find?
  • Conclusion and contribution: what does it add, and what are its limits?

Screening in three stages

Experienced researchers do not begin by reading a paper end to end. They screen in stages, spending more time on fewer papers each time.

  1. Title and abstract. Papers unrelated to your question drop out here, usually about half of a hundred.
  2. Structured summary. Look at research question, method and findings. Most of the remainder drops out here.
  3. Full read. Read end to end and take notes only on papers that will genuinely enter your review.

Let AI do the middle stage

The AI Summarize tool recognizes academic text and gives a structured summary around research question, method, findings and conclusion. You can see whether a paper fits your review without reading it.

AI Summarize — See in seconds whether a paper is useful to you. Open the tool

With many papers, use AI Batch to summarize them all and gather the results in one document. Mind plagiarism and citation rules: a summary is not a substitute for reading the source and citing it correctly.

Do not skip the method section

However striking a finding looks, the method determines how strong it is. Treating a survey of fifty people and a longitudinal study of thousands as equally weighty is among the most criticized flaws in literature reviews. Check sample size, study design and data collection while reading the summary, and you avoid a hard defence later.

Limitations and conflicting findings

A good review does not just line up studies that agree. It also shows conflicting findings. A paper's own limitations section is the most valuable part for this, because it states the boundary the authors set around their work. Note it separately while summarizing and your discussion section becomes much easier to write.

Tie every note to its source

If you do not record which paper a sentence came from, you will hunt for the source again while writing. A practical layout is a one-line citation per paper, three or four summary bullets, and direct quotes with page numbers. Gathering batch output into one document makes this easy to maintain.

What a summary cannot do

A summary conveys what the paper claims, not whether the claim holds. Catching a statistical error, an unsuitable control group or an overreaching generalization is still the reader's job. Use summaries to speed up screening, but citing a paper you have not read is not academically defensible.

item.title: Turn Photos and Scans Into One PDF, Free in Your Browser
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Ten loose photos are awkward to send. One ordered PDF is not. Here is how to build it, and how to avoid the problems that make people send it twice.
item.content:encoded:
Whether it is photographed paperwork for an application, scanned receipts for expenses or pages for your archive, a single PDF is easier to send, print and keep than a pile of images.

Why a PDF beats separate images

One file with ordered pages looks more professional than several JPG or PNG attachments, prints more easily, and the recipient opens everything with one click.

Three steps

  1. Add images — Drag JPG or PNG files into the Image to PDF tool, up to 80 MB.
  2. Set the order — Arrange the images; each becomes a page.
  3. Download — Click Convert to PDF and the file is ready immediately.

Image to PDF — Combine photos and scans into one PDF for free. Open the tool

The tool runs entirely in your browser. Your images stay on your device and are never uploaded.

Check the photos first

Images go into the PDF exactly as they are, because the tool does not repair the photo. Quality is decided when you take the shot, and a quick check is faster than sending the file twice.

  • Keep all four edges of the document in frame; a cut-off edge gets files rejected.
  • Avoid shadows and glare, and light the page from the front rather than the side.
  • Shoot straight on, because a skewed photo stays skewed in the PDF.
  • Make sure the text is legible; if you struggle on screen, so will the recipient.

If your photos are skewed or shadowed, the Document Scanner gives a better result than converting directly. It detects the edges and corrects perspective, so the output looks like it came from a scanner.

Mind the page order

Your gallery sorts by capture time, which often differs from the document's logical order, and fronts and backs of double-sided paperwork get mixed up most. Review the order once from start to finish before converting.

When the file is too large

One photo from a recent phone can be 3 to 5 MB, so ten pages reach 30 to 50 MB and exceed the 20 to 25 MB attachment limit of most email services. Do not degrade the shots; run the finished PDF through the compress tool instead, where gains on scanned material are usually substantial.

Making the text searchable

In a PDF built from images the text is a picture, so you cannot search or copy it. Run the PDF through OCR to add an invisible text layer. Ctrl+F then works and the appearance stays the same.

JPG or PNG?

JPG suits photographed paperwork and keeps files small. For screenshots, charts and sharp lines, PNG looks cleaner because its compression is lossless, at the cost of size. Mixing both in one PDF is fine.

item.title: Month-End Invoice Batch: PDFs Ready for Your Accountant
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: The time saving is not only in the extraction. It comes from tidying the folder before and checking the table after. A practical month-end routine.
item.content:encoded:
For small businesses and freelancers, month-end often means opening PDF invoices one at a time and keying them into a sheet. Batch processing handles the lot in one pass, and a little preparation makes the result far more reliable.

What batch solves

One invoice is easy. The pain is dozens in a row. AI Batch works through a folder of invoices in turn, extracts each one's data (invoice number, date, seller, amount, VAT) and merges everything into one CSV with a row per invoice.

  1. Bulk-upload invoices — Add your PDF invoices to the AI Batch tool, up to 25 files.
  2. Choose Extract mode — Start the run and watch live progress for each invoice.
  3. Download one CSV — All invoices merge into one table, ready for Excel or your accounting import.

AI Batch — Process dozens of invoices at once and download one CSV. Open the tool

If scanned invoices are mixed in with text ones, OCR starts automatically. Still review critical amounts once.

Tidy the folder before you start

A month's invoices arrive as email attachments, in the downloads folder and as phone photos. Processing them as they are means an hour spent cleaning up the output.

  • Remove duplicate copies of the same invoice; double entry is the most common error.
  • Move non-invoice documents, such as delivery notes, quotes and bank receipts, to a separate folder.
  • Run photographed invoices through the Document Scanner first, because legibility improves noticeably.
  • Put dates in file names so you can match a row back to its invoice while checking.

Check the table with totals, not row by row

Reading dozens of rows one by one gives back the time you saved. Open the table in Excel and run a few aggregate checks instead: compare the amount column total with the period total, check VAT against the amounts, sort the dates and look for anything outside the period, and filter seller names for anyone unexpected. Opening the handful of rows that look odd is far more efficient than reading them all.

The invoices most likely to go wrong

  • Photographed invoices that are shadowed or skewed.
  • Foreign-language invoices with a different date order, such as month first.
  • Multi-line invoices, where the total may read correctly while the line breakdown is incomplete.
  • Documents with handwritten notes or stamps added.
  • Invoices with discounts, advances or credits, where sign errors show up.

Build the archive from the start

Invoices are needed not only at month-end but years later, in an audit or a warranty claim. Merge the month's invoices into one PDF, add page numbers and make it searchable, and you avoid hunting through a folder of separate files. One file per month means twelve files a year, an archive a person can actually manage.

Agree a format with your accountant

Accountants usually expect a particular column order, date format and file naming pattern. Settle that once in the first month and each later month takes minutes. Arrange the CSV columns to match and save that arrangement as a template.

item.title: PDF Too Big to Email? Compress It Without Visible Loss
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: A 'file too large' bounce usually traces back to images inside the PDF. Set realistic expectations, remove what you do not need, then compress.
item.content:encoded:
Email services typically cap attachments at 20 to 25 MB, and a scanned or image-heavy PDF passes that easily. Most PDFs can be reduced a lot with no loss you would notice.

Where the size comes from

Images dominate: high-resolution scans, photos and embedded pictures. Text takes almost no space, so compression mostly works by bringing images down to a sensible resolution.

Three steps

  1. Upload the PDF — Open the Compress tool and choose your file.
  2. Compress — The tool optimizes images and redundant data to reduce the size.
  3. Download the result — The smaller file fits an email or upload comfortably.

Compress PDF — Reduce your PDF's size and share it easily. Open the tool

The biggest gains come from scans. Text-only PDFs are already small, so savings there are limited.

Try deleting before compressing

In scanned files, blank reverse sides, pages scanned twice and pointless cover sheets can take several megabytes. Removing them with the delete-pages tool and then compressing beats compression alone, and costs no quality.

What to expect by file type

  • Scanned documents: the biggest gains. High-resolution scans usually shrink a lot.
  • Image-heavy decks and catalogues: good gains, but watch the setting if image quality matters.
  • Text-only documents: already small, so you will not turn a 400 KB contract into 100 KB.
  • Files compressed before: a second pass gains little and costs quality.

If compression is not enough

Split the document into sensible parts and send two emails; the recipient gets the parts in order. For statements or reports, sending only the relevant page range reduces size and avoids sharing information nobody asked for.

Checking quality

Compression shows in print and at zoom, not at normal screen size. After downloading, open the page with the smallest type and zoom to 200%. If the letters are still legible, the file is usable. Do not skip this for documents going to an institution, because an illegible scan is among the most common reasons for rejection.

Keep files small from the start

  • Scan at 300 DPI rather than 600; more is unnecessary for text documents.
  • Do not scan black-and-white paperwork in colour; greyscale is usually enough and far smaller.
  • Run phone photos through the Document Scanner instead of converting them to PDF directly.
  • Do not compress and re-save the same document repeatedly, since each round costs a little more quality.

item.title: PDF to Word: Edit a PDF Without Retyping It
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Converting to Word is the quickest way to rework a PDF's text. Here is what converts well, what does not, and how to avoid the usual formatting surprises.
item.content:encoded:
A PDF is made to be shared, not changed. When the text inside needs real rewriting, converting the file to Word is usually the shortest route.

Why direct editing is awkward

A PDF places text and columns at fixed positions, so changing one word can break the layout. In Word, paragraphs, headings and tables flow again and behave like any document.

Three steps

  1. Upload the PDF — Open the PDF to Word tool and choose your document.
  2. Convert — The tool analyzes text and layout and produces an editable .docx.
  3. Download and edit — Open it in Microsoft Word, Google Docs or similar.

Convert PDF to Word — Turn your PDF into an editable Word document. Open the tool

A scanned PDF needs OCR first. Without it the Word file holds a picture of the page instead of text you can edit.

What converts cleanly

Quality depends on how the PDF was made. A report written in Word and saved as PDF comes back almost perfectly, while a catalogue designed in graphics software will not.

  • Very well: single-column, text-heavy reports, letters and contracts.
  • Well: documents with simple tables and numbered headings.
  • Poorly: multi-column magazine layouts, nested tables and heavy text-box use.
  • Not at all: scans, which need OCR first or the Word file just contains an image.

A short checklist after converting

A glance at a few things in Word prevents surprises later, and it matters most on anything going to someone else.

  • Tables: are rows and columns split or cells merged unexpectedly?
  • Heading levels: are the styles right if you will build an automatic contents page?
  • Page breaks: does anything split mid-paragraph?
  • Accented characters: did they survive?
  • Page numbers: numbers baked in as text will clash with Word's own.

The right order for scans

In a scanned PDF each page is a photograph, so converting straight to Word gives you an image. Run OCR first to make the text searchable, then convert. If the scan is poor, rotating and removing shadows beforehand noticeably improves recognition.

When editing the PDF directly is better

If only a date, amount or name changes, a round trip through Word and back to PDF is more work than the job deserves, and each pass nudges the formatting. Editing the PDF text directly leaves the rest untouched. For substantial rewriting, Word is the right call.

Going back to PDF

Official submissions often do not accept Word files, so you will need a PDF again. Watch fonts on that step: a typeface not installed elsewhere can look right to you and different to the recipient. Standard fonts remove that risk.

item.title: OCR Explained: Make a Scanned PDF Searchable
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: A scanned PDF is a stack of photographs of text. OCR reads those photographs and gives the words back to you. Here is what affects the result.
item.content:encoded:
Scan a document into a PDF and the writing on the page is really a picture. That is why you cannot select, search or copy it. OCR, short for optical character recognition, reads the picture and turns it back into real text.

What OCR does

It recognizes the letters and words in the page image and converts them into editable, searchable text. A scanned contract, deed or invoice can then be searched, copied or summarized.

Three steps

  1. Upload the scanned PDF — Add your photo or scan-based PDF to the OCR tool.
  2. Convert to text — OCR turns the text in the page images into real text on your device (Turkish and English).
  3. Use the text — Search it, copy it, or feed it into the summarize and translate tools.

Scanned PDF to Text (OCR) — Turn text in a scanned document into real text. Open the tool

Processing happens entirely on your device and the document is not uploaded. Clear, high-resolution scans give the best results.

What decides accuracy

The same engine can be near-perfect on a clean scan and confused by a shadowed phone photo. The main factors are:

  • Resolution: scans around 300 DPI do noticeably better, and below 150 DPI the error rate climbs fast.
  • Contrast: faded ink or a grey photocopy makes letters hard to separate from the background.
  • Skew: even a few degrees of tilt disrupts line tracking.
  • Typeface: standard print faces are recognized well, while handwriting and decorative fonts are unreliable.
  • Layout: reading order can get scrambled on multi-column pages and tables.

Accented and non-English characters

Characters outside the basic Latin set are where OCR slips most often. The Turkish dotless i against the dotted one, or capital I with a dot against plain I, is a classic case. Where a single character matters, as in identity papers, deeds or contracts, verify the output by eye. For later searching, small errors are harmless; for copying into something official, checking is essential.

Searchable PDF or plain text?

These are two different needs. A searchable PDF places an invisible text layer over the page, so the document looks identical but Ctrl+F works. Plain text suits moving the words elsewhere, but the page layout is lost. Most people find the searchable PDF more useful because the document keeps its official look.

Prepare the document first

A little preparation noticeably improves recognition. Straighten skewed pages with the rotate tool, delete blank or duplicate pages, and run phone photos through the Document Scanner first, because it finds the edges and corrects perspective so OCR receives a much cleaner page.

What you can do afterwards

  • Export the document to Word and edit it.
  • Have AI summarize a long contract.
  • Pull amounts and dates from an invoice into a table.
  • Translate the document into another language.
  • Find it years later in your archive with a single keyword.

item.title: Lease Agreement Checklist: Deposit, Rent, Move-Out Traps
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: Most tenancy disputes begin at move-out and revolve around the deposit. A short list of clauses and one set of photos can prevent nearly all of them.
item.content:encoded:
A lease can look standard and still hide the clauses that cause the biggest fights: how the deposit is returned, how the rent rises, and how a tenancy ends. Read these points before you sign, not after the first dispute.

The short checklist

  • Rent amount, payment day and method.
  • Rent increase rate and the index it is tied to.
  • Deposit amount and return conditions.
  • Term, renewal and termination clauses.
  • Who is responsible for dues, bills and repairs.
  • Eviction conditions and notice periods.
  • An inventory list and a record of existing damage.

Deposit: where disputes begin

Disagreements rarely happen at move-in. They happen at move-out, almost always about the deposit. If the agreement does not state when, under what conditions and with which deductions it is returned, the outcome depends on what each side remembers. Make sure three things are written: the return period, the situations that allow deductions, and that ordinary wear and tear is not deductible.

Record the condition on moving day

The answer to a deposit dispute is usually a few photos taken on day one. Photograph paint, flooring, kitchen units, bathroom fittings and any scratches or stains, and note the meter readings. Turn the images into a single PDF and attach it to an inventory list signed by both sides. That is far stronger evidence than memory two years later.

What is the rent increase tied to?

The increase clause is often one line, yet it governs the most money. Is it a fixed percentage or tied to an index, and which period's figures apply? Statutory caps are also judged against this clause. Clarify any ambiguity before signing, because it is far easier than arguing a year later.

Who pays for what?

  • Service charges: which items, such as heating, cleaning and the lift, fall to the tenant?
  • Major repairs to fixtures are usually the landlord's responsibility.
  • Maintenance of the boiler, air conditioning and appliances should be stated explicitly.
  • Whose name are the utility accounts in, and who transfers them at the end?
  • Permission to redecorate: changes made without written consent cause problems at move-out.

Term, renewal and notice

How and when an agreement ends matters as much as how it starts. Missing the notice period can commit you to another term you did not want. On the day you sign, put the notice date in your calendar.

Ask the contract questions

Finding one clause in a long contract takes time. With AI Chat you can upload the lease and ask directly, for example what the rent increase is tied to or when the deposit is returned. The AI answers based only on the contract.

Ask Your Contract — Upload the lease and ask about the clause you care about. Open AI Chat

AI helps you understand the contract. For legal validity and disputes, consult a lawyer; this tool is not a substitute for legal advice.

Keep the signed copy findable

A lease is requested in many places, from housing benefit applications to tax filings. Merge photos of the signed copy into one PDF and make it searchable, so one keyword finds it years later. If you share it with a third party, permanently remove unnecessary details such as identity numbers.

item.title: Understanding a Contract in a Language You Don't Speak
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: You do not need to read every line. Translate, summarize, then spend your attention on the handful of clauses where the risk sits.
item.content:encoded:
Contracts, proposals and technical documents often arrive in a language you do not read well. Translating every line with a dictionary is slow. A better routine is to translate the document with its structure intact, summarize it, and then concentrate on the few clauses that matter.

Translate, then summarize

Do it in two steps: translate the document into your language, and if it is long, summarize the key points. Translation keeps headings, lists and tables, and the summary brings forward parties, dates and obligations.

  1. Translate the document — Upload the PDF to AI Translate and pick a target language. It keeps the structure and you can download a PDF.
  2. Summarize if long — Use AI Summarize for the key points, parties and critical clauses of the translated document.
  3. Ask about tricky parts — Use AI Chat to ask directly about a clause you want to understand.

AI Translate — Translate a foreign-language document while preserving structure. Open the tool

AI translation is for fast comprehension. Documents that need official or legal validity require a sworn translator.

Where to look first

Reading the whole contract is usually unnecessary, because the real risk concentrates in a few clauses. Most commercial contracts use similar headings:

  • Parties and authority: who signs, and does the document show their authority?
  • Term and renewal: does it renew automatically, and how much notice prevents that?
  • Termination: in what circumstances and with how much notice can it end?
  • Payment: amount, currency, due dates and late interest.
  • Liability cap and indemnity: is there an upper limit on damages?
  • Governing law and jurisdiction: where and under which law are disputes resolved?
  • Confidentiality and non-compete: duration and scope.

Why governing law deserves attention

The governing law and jurisdiction clause is near the end and often very short, yet in a dispute it can matter more than everything above it. Pursuing a claim in another country's courts can cost more than the work the contract covers. Do not skip it, and ask directly about anything unclear.

Mind the legal vocabulary

Some legal terms differ from everyday meaning, and a literal translation can mislead. In English contracts 'shall' expresses obligation while 'may' expresses discretion, and terms such as 'indemnify', 'warranty' and 'best efforts' carry meanings tied to a legal system. A translation tells you what the text says. Judging its legal effect is a separate job.

Comparing two versions

In negotiation the other side often sends an updated version and says the edits are minor. Rather than rereading everything, compare the two versions: added, removed and changed clauses appear one by one. This is how quiet changes to amounts, dates and liability get caught.

When you need a professional

AI translation and summaries help you understand a document and ask better questions. They do not replace a lawyer on contracts you will sign, that involve significant sums or that bind you for a long time. Official procedures require a sworn translation, and institutions do not accept machine translation.

item.title: PDF Passwords: How to Remove or Add One Safely
item.dc:creator: PDF Platform
item.description: A PDF can carry two very different kinds of password. Knowing which one you are dealing with decides what to remove, what to add and how to send it.
item.content:encoded:
People ask about PDF passwords for two opposite reasons: they want a password they already know gone for good, or they want to put one on a document before sharing it. Separate tools handle each, and a little background avoids the usual confusion.

Two passwords, two strengths

  • Open (user) password: needed to open the file at all. Without it the document cannot be viewed, because the content is genuinely encrypted.
  • Permissions (owner) password: the file opens without a prompt, but printing, copying or editing is restricted. That restriction is a flag the viewer chooses to respect, which is far weaker than encryption.

Someone who says their PDF is protected yet opens fine is dealing with the second kind, and that is usually the one that has to go before they can work with the document.

Removing a password you know

If a PDF asks for a password every time, the Unlock PDF tool removes it permanently. You must know the current password.

  1. Upload the PDF — Add your password-protected document to the Unlock PDF tool.
  2. Enter the password — Type the current password, and only for documents you are authorized to open.
  3. Download the unlocked file — The password is gone, so there is no prompt on each opening.

Unlock PDF — Remove a password you know and use the PDF freely. Open the tool

Adding a password

To protect a contract, medical report or financial document before sharing it, the Encrypt tool adds an open password so only people who know it can open the file.

Encrypt PDF — Add an open password to your sensitive document. Encrypt tool

Only remove passwords from documents you own or are explicitly authorized to unlock.

Which kind should you add?

Decide whether you want to stop people seeing the content or only stop them reusing it. Medical reports, financial statements and anything with identity data need an open password. A proposal or catalogue usually only needs protection against editing, and a permissions password is enough.

Sending the password safely

Putting the file and its password in the same email makes the protection pointless, because anyone who reads that email gets both. Send the file by email and the password by another channel, such as a phone call, a text message or a different app. Most corporate information-security policies require exactly this.

  • Do not put the password in the file name; contract-1234.pdf defeats the purpose.
  • Do not reuse one password across documents.
  • Avoid guessable strings such as birthdays or ID numbers.
  • If you forget the password the document cannot be opened, so keep a backup.

If you do not know the password

There is no legitimate way to open a file whose open password you do not know. That is the design of the protection, not a flaw. If the document is yours, ask the sender or the program that created it. Trying to defeat protection on someone else's document creates ethical and legal problems.

Clean up afterwards

An unlocked file is unprotected, and anyone can open it from a cloud backup, shared folder or mailbox. Keep the password off only as long as you need to work, delete the unprotected copy afterwards and add a password again if you share the document.
